Fire Fighting Robot Kit – Arduino UNO R3

blocks.text: The Fire Fighting Robot Kit for Arduino UNO R3 contains the parts to build a small robot that finds a flame and puts it out with water. A 5-channel flame sensor tells the Arduino where the fire is, the 2WD chassis drives toward it through an L298N motor driver, and a relay switches a mini water pump while an SG90 servo sweeps the hose. The kit contains 14 parts, 93 pieces in total.
Controller: Arduino UNO R3 compatible board (ATmega328P)
Drive: 2WD smart robot car chassis with L298N dual H-bridge driver
Extinguisher: mini submersible pump DC 3-6V, 1 m PVC hose (6 x 8 mm), 1-channel 5V relay module (active low), SG90 servo
Power: 2 x 18650 Li-ion cells (used) in a 2-cell holder, KDC-08 on/off switch
The Arduino reads the five flame sensor channels to find the strongest flame.
The motors turn the robot toward that side.
When the flame is near, the relay turns the pump on and the servo sweeps the water left and right.
digitalWrite(RELAY, LOW); // active low: pump ON

Run the pump within its 3-6V rating; do not connect it directly to the 7.4V battery pack.
Keep water away from the electronics, and test with a small candle only, under adult supervision, away from anything flammable.

name: Obstacle Avoiding Robot Car Kit 4WD – Arduino UNO

blocks.text: The Obstacle Avoiding Robot Car Kit 4WD is a complete set of parts for building an Arduino UNO robot that drives on its own and steers away from walls and objects. An HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor on an SG90 servo looks ahead and to the sides, the Arduino decides which way is clear, and an L298N driver runs the motors of the 4WD acrylic chassis. The kit contains 12 parts, 91 pieces in total.
Controller: Arduino UNO R3 compatible board (ATmega328P)
Distance sensor: HC-SR04 ultrasonic, 2 to 400 cm
Motor driver: L298N dual H-bridge module
Chassis: 4WD transparent acrylic robot car chassis kit
Power: 2 x 18650 Li-ion cells in a 2-cell holder (about 7.4V nominal), with a KDC-08 rocker on/off switch
The Arduino sends a 10 µs pulse to the HC-SR04 TRIG pin and measures the ECHO pulse width.
Distance in cm ≈ echo time in µs ÷ 58.
If an obstacle is closer than a set limit (for example 20 cm), the robot stops, the servo turns the sensor left and right, and the car turns toward the side with more space.

blocks.text: The PCB FR2 Circuit Board 15 x 10 cm (Pointing / dot type) is a single-sided prototyping board made of FR2 phenolic paper laminate, with independent copper pads on a standard 2.54 mm (0.1") grid. It turns a breadboard experiment into a permanent soldered circuit without ordering a custom PCB. The larger working area suits medium and larger projects.
Copper: single-sided, separate dots (pads), no pre-connected tracks
Hole pitch: 2.54 mm, hole diameter about 1.0 mm
Plan the layout first, ideally after testing the circuit on a breadboard.
Insert through-hole parts from the plain side and solder each lead to its pad on the copper side.
Connect pads with solder bridges, bent component leads or short pieces of wire.
Check for unwanted bridges between neighbouring pads with a multimeter in continuity mode before powering up.
Permanent versions of Arduino and microcontroller projects
Sensor, driver, power regulator and LED circuits
The 2.54 mm pitch fits DIP ICs, IC sockets, pin headers and most through-hole parts.
FR2 is easy to cut: score both sides along a row of holes and snap, or use a fine saw.
Use moderate iron temperature and short contact time; FR2 pads can lift if overheated.

blocks.text: The DT9205A Digital Multimeter (basic model MT-1000) is an easy-to-use handheld meter with a large 3½-digit LCD. It covers the everyday measurements needed on the bench and in the field: AC/DC voltage, AC/DC current, resistance, capacitance, diode test, transistor hFE and an audible continuity buzzer. A rubber holster with a tilt stand makes it practical for daily use in electronics and electrical work.
DC / AC current: up to 20A (fused ranges)
Other tests: diode, transistor hFE, continuity buzzer, data hold
Black probe always in COM. Red probe in VΩ for voltage, resistance and diode tests.
For current, move the red probe to the mA or 20A jack and connect the meter in series with the load.
Start on the highest range and step down until you get a clear reading.

Electronics repair, Arduino and hobby projects

The load seen by a crystal is (C1 × C2) ÷ (C1 + C2) + stray capacitance. With two 15pF capacitors in series give 7.5pF, plus roughly 3 to 5pF of board and pin capacitance, for a total load of about 11 to 12pF, which suits crystals specified for about 12pF load. Always check the load capacitance in your crystal’s datasheet.

The 10pF 50V ceramic capacitor is a small through-hole capacitor used in high-frequency and timing circuits. Very low values like 10pF are typical around crystals and oscillators, in RF and antenna circuits, and for filtering fast noise on signal lines. Ceramic capacitors are non-polarized, so they can be fitted either way round.
Typical marking: 100 (10 followed by no zeros = 10pF)

Ceramic capacitors use a three-digit code in picofarads: the first two digits are the value and the third digit is the number of zeros. So 100 means 10pF, 220 means 22pF and 104 means 100,000pF (100nF).

A crystal oscillator usually has one capacitor from each crystal pin to GND. Two 10pF capacitors in this position give 10 × 10 ÷ (10 + 10) = 5pF, plus a few pF of board stray capacitance, which suits crystals specified for a load of about 8pF to 10pF. Always check the load capacitance in your crystal’s datasheet; many 16 MHz Arduino crystals use 22pF instead.
High-frequency noise filtering on signal lines
Op-amp feedback compensation to prevent oscillation
Keep the leads short and place the capacitor close to the pins it serves; long leads add inductance and stray capacitance.

This 4pF ceramic capacitor rated 50V is a small-value through-hole capacitor for high-frequency and precision timing circuits. Values in the low picofarad range are used where only a tiny amount of capacitance is needed, such as tuning RF circuits, fine-adjusting oscillators and filtering very high frequencies. Ceramic capacitors are non-polarised, so they can be fitted either way round.
RF tuning and matching networks in radio and wireless circuits
Fine adjustment of oscillator and crystal circuits
Compensation capacitors in amplifier feedback loops
Keep the leads as short as possible: at high frequencies even a few millimetres of wire add inductance and stray capacitance comparable to 4pF.
PCB tracks, breadboards and probes add a few picofarads of stray capacitance, so circuits using such small values behave best on a compact, well-laid-out PCB.
Stay below the 50V rating with a margin; in low-voltage Arduino and RF projects this is easily met.
When replacing a capacitor in a tuned circuit, use the same value so the frequency does not shift.

1pF is one millionth of a microfarad (1pF = 0.000001µF). Small ceramic capacitors are often marked with a short code instead of the full value, so check the marking against the value you need before soldering.

blocks.text: The 12V 5A power adapter is a 60W switching AC-DC supply that converts mains power (100–240V AC) into a regulated 12V DC output. It is the standard supply for LED strips, CCTV cameras, routers, motors and many hobby and industrial boards that need a solid 12V rail.
Connector: 5.5 × 2.1mm DC barrel plug, centre positive
Protection: over-voltage, over-current and short-circuit protection

Add up the current of everything on the 12V output and keep it at about 80% of the rating for long, cool operation: 5A × 0.8 = 4A, or about 48W. For example, a 12V LED strip rated 14.4W per metre (1.2A per metre) can run about 3 metres comfortably from this adapter.
CCTV cameras, DVR/NVR recorders and routers
Arduino and Raspberry Pi projects through a 12V-to-5V buck converter
Check the polarity of your device: this adapter is centre positive.
For long LED strip runs, feed power at both ends to avoid voltage drop.
Leave space around the adapter for air flow; it gets warm at full load.
The adapter connects to mains voltage. Do not open it, keep it dry, and replace it if the cable or housing is damaged.

blocks.text: زرار وجرس وضوء لإرسال رسايل بشفرة مورس بإيدك، مع بطاقة لتعليم رموز الحروف.
ده كيت يدوي من غير برمجة (مختلف عن كيت الإرسال الضوئي اللي بيستخدم أردوينو). لما الطفل يدوس الزرار، الجرس بيصفّر والليد بينوّر. موديول الطاقة بيحوّل 9 فولت لـ 5 فولت وفيه مفتاح تشغيل.
الدائرة على التوازي (جرس وليد مع بعض)
النقطة (•) = ضغطة قصيرة، والشرطة (—) = ضغطة أطول 3 مرات. سيب مسافة صغيرة بين الحروف ومسافة أكبر بين الكلمات. جرّب: SOS = ••• ——— •••
ركّب موديول الطاقة على طرف البريدبورد ووصّل البطارية في مشبكه.
من خرج 5 فولت للزرار، ومن الزرار للجرس، وكمان لمقاومة 220 أوم ثم الليد.
مفيش صوت: اتأكد من اتجاه الجرس (الرجل الطويلة +).
اتأكد إن مفتاح موديول الطاقة على ON.

blocks.text: كيت تعليمي يخلّي الطفل يبني نظام ري صغير بيقيس رطوبة التربة ويشغّل مضخة مياه لوحده لما الزرعة تعطش.

حساس رطوبة التربة السعوي (Capacitive) بيقيس نسبة المية في التربة، والأردوينو يقرر: لو التربة ناشفة يشغّل المضخة عن طريق الريلاي لمدة قصيرة، ويستنى المية تتشرب، وبعدين يقيس تاني. المضخة بتاخد كهرباء من مصدر 5V منفصل (أدابتر 5V 2A مع موديول دخل للبريدبورد فيه مفتاح تشغيل)، ومش بتتشغل أبدًا من رجل الأردوينو مباشرة.

name: MAX485 TTL to RS485 Converter Module – Serial Transceiver Board for Arduino & Microcontrollers

blocks.text: The MAX485 TTL to RS-485 Converter Module lets a microcontroller such as an Arduino communicate over an industrial RS-485 bus. Based on the MAX485 half-duplex transceiver, it converts the UART TX/RX lines into the differential A/B pair, giving reliable communication over long cables, in electrically noisy places and between many devices on the same two wires, for example Modbus RTU, DMX512 and sensor networks.
Bus: up to 32 devices; cable runs up to about 1200 m at lower data rates
DI: driver input, connect to the microcontroller TX
RO: receiver output, connect to the microcontroller RX
RE: receiver enable, active LOW (LOW = receive)
A / B: RS-485 bus pair (screw terminal)
Tie DE and RE together to one Arduino pin: HIGH to transmit, LOW to receive. Connect A to A and B to B on every device, preferably with twisted-pair cable, and share a ground between devices.
Arduino Uno with SoftwareSerial on pins 10 (RX, to RO) and 11 (TX, to DI), DE + RE on pin 2:
void loop() { digitalWrite(2, HIGH); rs485.print("Hello"); digitalWrite(2, LOW); delay(1000); }

Long-distance sensor networks and home automation

blocks.text: This high-power DC-DC boost converter steps a lower DC voltage up to an adjustable output of up to 50V, rated 250W and 10A. Keep the current within the 10A rating. Reaching the full 250W needs a higher input voltage, because at 12V input 10A is only about 120W.

The TCA9548A module is a 1-to-8 I2C multiplexer. It sits between your microcontroller and up to 8 separate I2C buses, so you can connect several devices that share the same fixed address, such as identical OLED displays or sensors, and talk to them one at a time. It is controlled over I2C itself, so it only needs the SDA and SCL pins of your Arduino, ESP32 or Raspberry Pi.

SDA / SCL: to the microcontroller I2C bus
RST: reset, leave unconnected or pull high in normal use
SD0–SD7 / SC0–SC7: the 8 downstream I2C channels
Select a channel by writing one bit to the multiplexer:
void tcaSelect(uint8_t ch) { Wire.beginTransmission(0x70); Wire.write(1 << ch); Wire.endTransmission(); }
Call tcaSelect(0); before talking to the device on channel 0, then tcaSelect(1); for the next one, and so on.

blocks.text: The 82D05 is a 12V Class-D digital power amplifier module, using the same efficient switching-amplification principle found in modern compact audio gear: rather than continuously varying its output like an older analog amplifier, it rapidly switches its output on and off to reproduce the audio waveform, which lets it deliver real audio power while running cool and drawing comparatively little wasted energy as heat – a meaningful advantage when a design runs from a 12V DC supply or battery rather than mains power.

Running from 12V rather than a lower 5V USB-style supply gives this module more headroom to drive larger, more demanding speakers than a typical 5V amplifier board can comfortably handle, making it a popular choice for DIY Bluetooth speaker builds – commonly paired with a separate Bluetooth audio receiver module to provide the wireless input – small PA/announcement speaker projects, and general 12V-powered audio amplification builds.

blocks.text: The HW-357 combines two functions that are normally handled by separate modules: it charges a connected battery (typically a single-cell lithium battery) from an external input, and it also includes an integrated step-up (boost) converter to raise that battery’s voltage back up to a stable, usable output level for powering a device – the same core idea behind a basic power bank, packed onto one small board.

This kind of combined charge-and-boost design is popular in portable, battery-powered DIY builds because it removes the need to wire together a separate charging module and a separate boost converter, reducing both part count and wiring complexity. It’s a practical building block for projects that need to run from a rechargeable battery while still delivering a steady, higher output voltage to the rest of the circuit.
Combines battery charging and voltage step-up (boost) in one module
Reduces part count versus separate charger + boost modules
Common use: DIY power banks, portable battery-powered electronics

blocks.text: This is a single replacement soldering iron tip in the widely-used 900M series, a standard tip form-factor compatible with a large range of soldering irons and stations built around the same tip mount – meaning it isn’t limited to one specific iron brand. Over time, a soldering tip’s working surface oxidizes and wears from repeated heat cycling and solder contact; swapping in a fresh tip restores clean, efficient heat transfer to the joint far more cheaply than replacing the whole iron.

Sold as a single piece, it’s the practical option when only one specific tip needs replacing rather than restocking multiple spares at once – handy for keeping a soldering station running as soon as its current tip starts showing signs of wear.
Compatible with 900M-standard soldering irons and stations
Replaces worn or oxidized tips to keep an existing iron usable

name: DS-430 Square Momentary Push Button Switch 2-Pin
desc: DS-430 Square Push Button Switch 1. Type: Momentary Push Button 2. Shape: Square 3. Pins: 2 4. Model: DS-430 5. Mounting: PCB / Through-hole

blocks.text: The DS-430 is a compact square-bodied momentary push button with a simple 2-pin contact – pressing the button closes the circuit between its two pins, and releasing it opens the circuit again, with no latching or held state. This 2-terminal design keeps wiring simple: unlike 4-pin tactile buttons where pin pairing can be a common source of wiring mistakes, a 2-pin button has only one possible way to wire it, reducing the chance of an accidental short or dead connection during assembly.

Its square profile and small footprint make it well suited to PCB-mounted designs and compact enclosures where a low-profile manual trigger is needed – common uses include reset buttons, manual trigger inputs for microcontroller projects, and simple one-shot control actions in DIY electronics builds.
Common uses: reset buttons, manual trigger inputs, simple control actions

blocks.text: The LA38 is a heavy-duty momentary push button built to the standard 22mm industrial panel-mount size, the same cutout diameter used across most industrial control panels, machine enclosures, and DIY control boxes – meaning it drops into standard 22mm mounting holes without needing a custom cutout. As a momentary switch, it only closes its contact while actually being pressed, springing back to rest the instant it’s released, making it suited to start/trigger-style actions rather than a latching ON/OFF state.

Its heavy-duty construction is built for frequent actuation and panel-mount durability well beyond what a small PCB tactile button is rated for, making it a common choice for control panels and enclosure-mounted manual triggers – green is conventionally used for start, go, or confirm-style actions on a panel.
Actuation: Momentary (returns to rest position when released)

desc: TNI-U Wire Cutter TU-109 1. Type: Diagonal Wire Cutter 2. Brand: TNI-U 3. Model: TU-109 4. Use: Cutting wires, component leads 5. Build: Precision hand tool

blocks.text: The TNI-U TU-109 is a precision hand-held wire cutter built for cleanly trimming wires, component leads, and small-gauge cable during electronics assembly and repair. Its hardened jaws shear through wire in a single squeeze, leaving a flush, low-burr cut – which matters both for a tidy finished build and for avoiding sharp leftover wire stubs that can short against neighboring parts on a crowded PCB.

Like any manual cutter, it needs no power or setup beyond consistent hand pressure, making it a natural companion to pliers, tweezers, and a soldering iron on any electronics workbench – useful for everything from trimming leads flush after soldering to cutting jumper wires to length.
Use: Trimming wires, component leads, small cables

name: SK12D07VG3 Right-Angle SPDT Slide Switch 50V 0.5A PCB Mount
desc: SK12D07VG3 Slide Switch (Right-Angle SPDT) 1. Type: Right-Angle Slide Switch 2. Circuit: SPDT (Single Pole Double Throw) 3. Rating: 50V, 0.5A 4. Mounting: PCB Plug-in (right-angle) 5. Model: SK12D07VG3

blocks.text: The SK12D07VG3 is a right-angle SPDT slide switch designed to mount flat against a PCB edge rather than standing upright, letting the actuator lever be accessed from the side of an enclosure while the switch body itself sits low and flush on the board – a common requirement for compact handheld devices and instruments where panel space is at a premium. Like any SPDT slide switch, moving the actuator connects the common pin to one of two output positions, giving a simple, latching two-state selection with no electronics or power needed to operate it.

Rated for 50V at 0.5A, it’s suited to low-voltage signal and small-load switching duties typical of hobby electronics and instrumentation – well beyond what’s needed for logic-level signal routing, with enough headroom for small indicator LEDs or low-current control lines.
Compact, low-profile footprint for panel-space-constrained builds

blocks.text: The ESP32-CAM-MB is the Micro USB programmer (download board) made for the ESP32-CAM. The ESP32-CAM has no USB port of its own, so it normally needs a separate USB-to-TTL adapter, jumper wires and a GPIO0-to-GND link every time you upload code. Simply plug the ESP32-CAM onto the ESP32-CAM-MB’s headers and connect one Micro USB cable: you get the serial connection for uploading from the Arduino IDE, a stable 5V supply and automatic reset / flash-mode switching.

name: 4-Way Arcade Joystick for DIY Arcade Sticks
desc: 4-Way Arcade Joystick 1. Type: Mechanical Arcade Joystick 2. Directions: 4-Way (Up / Down / Left / Right) 3. Switch Type: Microswitch-based 4. Mounting: Panel mount 5. Use: DIY arcade sticks & custom controllers

blocks.text: An arcade joystick translates the physical movement of its lever into electrical signals using a set of internal microswitches – one for each direction – so that pushing the stick toward a direction physically presses the corresponding microswitch closed. This 4-way version restricts movement to the four cardinal directions (up, down, left, right) rather than allowing diagonal travel, which suits games and controllers designed around strict 4-directional movement rather than the 8-way diagonal movement some other arcade titles expect.

Being a purely mechanical, switch-based input, it connects easily to a USB game controller encoder board (such as a “Zero Delay” style encoder) or directly to a microcontroller’s digital input pins for a custom-built controller, making it a common choice for DIY arcade cabinet projects, custom fight sticks, and MAME-based builds where a genuine arcade-feel joystick matters more than one sourced from a mass-market gamepad.
Mounting: Standard panel mount for arcade cabinets/enclosures
Compatible with USB encoder boards and microcontroller inputs
Built for DIY arcade sticks, custom controllers, and MAME cabinets
Durable mechanical design for repeated gameplay use

name: LM35 Temperature Sensor Module
desc: LM35 Module Temperature Sensor 1. Type: Analog Temperature Sensor 2. Output: 10mV per °C 3. Voltage: 4V – 20V DC 4. Current: < 60µA 5. Range: -55°C to +150°C

blocks.text: The LM35 module is a precision temperature sensor that outputs an analog voltage directly proportional to the Celsius temperature scale. It eliminates the need for external calibration or trimming, providing a reliable and linear output for embedded systems and microcontroller-based projects. The module typically includes the LM35 IC alongside supporting passive components, offering a simple interface for temperature measurement.

Operating with a voltage range of 4-20V DC, the sensor draws a low quiescent current of less than 60µA, ensuring minimal power consumption. Its output voltage changes by 10mV per degree Celsius, enabling direct reading without complex mathematical conversions. The sensor’s linear scale and predictable response make it suitable for a wide range of thermal monitoring applications where accuracy and stability are prioritized over absolute precision.
Minimal external components required for operation
Standard analog output interface for easy integration

name: XL4106 8A Buck Converter Module with Adjustable Voltage and Current
desc: Buck 8A XL4106 with Voltage and Current Adjustment 1. Max Current: 8A 2. Topology: Step-Down (Buck) 3. Control: CV/CC with pot adjustment 4. Efficiency: Up to 92% 5. Protection: Over-temperature

blocks.text: The Buck 8A XL4106 is a high-current, step-down DC-DC converter module featuring adjustable output voltage and current limiting. Based on the XL4106 switching regulator IC, it efficiently converts higher input voltages to lower output voltages while delivering up to 8A of continuous current. The onboard potentiometers enable user adjustment of both the output voltage and current threshold, making it suitable for powering demanding loads where precise control is required.

This module employs a constant-voltage, constant-current (CV/CC) control mechanism, allowing it to function as a general-purpose power supply or a dedicated battery charger. The current adjustment feature provides protection against overloads, limiting the maximum current drawn by the load. Its robust design and high conversion efficiency help reduce heat dissipation, ensuring stable operation under sustained load conditions.
Adjustable output voltage via onboard potentiometer
Adjustable current limiting via onboard potentiometer

name: GA12-N20 Mini DC Motor 12V 300 RPM
desc: Tiny DC Motor 12V 300 RPM GA12-N20 1. Voltage: 12V DC 2. Speed: 300 RPM (no-load) 3. Type: DC geared motor 4. Gearbox: GA12-N20 5. Gear Material: Metal

blocks.text: The Tiny DC Motor GA12-N20 is a compact, geared DC motor designed for portable and space-limited applications. It operates at a nominal 12V DC, delivering a rated output speed of 300 RPM. The integrated gearbox provides high torque at low speeds, making it suitable for driving wheels, small robotic actuators, and other mechanical elements where space efficiency is a priority.

This motor employs a brushed DC architecture with a metal gear train. The gears provide a mechanical advantage, converting high-speed, low-torque armature rotation into lower-speed, higher-torque output. Its miniature form factor, combined with the standard 12V operating voltage, allows for easy powering from common battery packs or regulated power supplies commonly found in hobbyist and educational projects.

Quiet operation due to precision gearing

name: 74266 Quad 2-Input XNOR Gate IC
desc: 74266 XNOR Gate IC 1. Function: Quad 2-input XNOR 2. Logic Family: 74LS/74HC compatible 3. Supply Voltage: 5V (typical) 4. Number of Gates: 4 5. Propagation Delay: ~10-20 ns

blocks.text: The 74266 XNOR gate IC is a quadruple 2-input XNOR logic gate, part of the standard 74LS or 74HC logic family. It provides the logical equivalence function, producing a high output when both inputs are the same (both high or both low). This chip is fundamental for digital logic design, used in comparators, parity checkers, and arithmetic circuits where equality detection is necessary.

Each of the four independent gates processes two digital inputs and outputs a single logic level. The device is typically powered by a 5V supply (for TTL versions) and offers standard noise margins and propagation delays compatible with other TTL logic devices. Its DIP or surface-mount packaging ensures easy integration into breadboards and printed circuit boards for educational and prototyping purposes.
Widely used in equality comparison circuits

blocks.text: The Robotica Level 2 Arduino Starter Kit is a complete hardware bundle built around the Arduino Uno R3 microcontroller board, designed for makers who have moved past basic tutorials and want to build powered, autonomous robotics projects. Rather than a single sensor or module, it’s a pre-matched set of the core subsystems a rolling robot needs: a brain, a power supply, and a motor driver.

Power is handled by an 18650 lithium-ion cell setup fitted with a rocker switch, giving the robot an onboard, rechargeable, disconnectable power source instead of relying on a wall adapter — a requirement for anything that needs to move freely. Motor control runs through an L298N Dual H-Bridge driver, which lets the Arduino switch and reverse two DC motors independently, enabling forward, reverse, and differential-steering (turn-in-place) behavior.

The Arduino Uno R3 itself acts as the programmable core, reading sensors and driving the L298N’s control pins according to whatever logic the builder programs — line following, obstacle avoidance, remote control, etc. A USB cable is included for both programming the Uno and, on many setups, initial power during development.

The IRF520 MOSFET Driver Module is an essential break-out board designed to bridge low-power microcontrollers with high-power DC peripherals. Perfect for DIY electronics, robotics, and automation setups, this module allows devices like an Arduino, Raspberry Pi, or ESP32 to safely control high-current loads that exceed their native GPIO pin limitations.

Equipped with a robust IRF520N Power MOSFET, the board utilizes a pulse-width modulation (PWM) or standard digital signal to smoothly control DC motors, high-power LED strips, solenoid valves, or miniature heating elements. The module features an onboard status LED to give immediate visual feedback of the output state, and heavy-duty screw terminals to ensure secure, low-resistance wiring connections.

blocks.v: Up to 5A (Requires an external heatsink & proper thermal management)

blocks.text: SIG (Signal): Input trigger pin connected to the microcontroller’s GPIO/PWM output pin.
VCC: Power input for the onboard circuitry (typically 5V or 3.3V matching logic level).
GND: Common ground connection shared with the microcontroller.
VIN / GND (Terminal 1): Connects to the external power supply for the high-power load (0V to 24V).
V+ / V- (Terminal 2): Connects directly to the target DC peripheral (e.g., motor, LED strip).
PWM Speed & Dimming Control: Seamlessly handles PWM signal streams, enabling precise speed control for DC motors or smooth brightness dimming for LED strings.
Microcontroller Protection: Acts as an electrical buffer, isolating your sensitive development board’s logic lines from high-voltage supply noises.
Onboard State LED Indicator: Includes a miniature surface-mount LED that illuminates when the control signal is high, streamlining rapid circuit debugging and validation.
Compact, Mountable Footprint: Features dual mechanical M3 mounting holes for solid fastening into custom control boxes or 3D-printed project enclosures.

Technical Note: For logic level inputs of 3.3V (e.g., ESP32 or Raspberry Pi Pico), the maximum output current will be significantly lower because the IRF520 is not a logic-level MOSFET and requires closer to 5V at the gate to fully open the channel. If driving loads above 1A, an external heatsink is strictly required.

name: HW-122 AMS1117 3.3V Power Module Board
desc: AMS1117 3.3V Power Module Board HW-122 1. Main Chip: AMS1117-3.3 2. Output Voltage: 3.3V (Fixed) 3. Max Output Current: 800mA 4. Input Voltage: 4.5V ~ 12V DC 5. Dropout Voltage: ~1V ~ 1.3V

blocks.text: The HW-122 is a small power module built around the AMS1117-3.3 low-dropout (LDO) linear regulator. It converts a 4.5V to 12V DC input into a stable 3.3V output, ideal for powering ESP8266 and ESP32 modules, NRF24L01 radios, sensors and other 3.3V devices from a 5V USB supply or a battery pack. On-board filter capacitors and a red power LED make it ready to use.
Pins: VIN, GND, VOUT, GND (2.54mm pitch)
On board: SMD filter capacitors and red power LED
VIN: to the input supply, for example 5V from USB or an Arduino 5V pin
GND: to the ground of the supply and of the 3.3V device (common ground)
VOUT: to the 3.3V / VCC pin of your module or sensor

A linear regulator turns the extra voltage into heat: P = (Vin − 3.3V) × I. From 5V at 300mA: (5 − 3.3) × 0.3 ≈ 0.5W, which this small board handles. From 12V at 300mA: (12 − 3.3) × 0.3 ≈ 2.6W, which is too much heat. For high currents, feed the module from 5V or use a buck converter from 12V.
3.3V sensors, displays and SD card modules
Add a 10µF to 100µF capacitor near Wi-Fi modules to cover their short current peaks.

name: XL4015 Step-Down Buck Converter with Digital Display
desc: XL4015 Step Down Buck Converter with Digital Display 1. Main Chip: XL4015 2. Output Current: Up to 5A 3. Output Power: 75W (Max) 4. Output Voltage: 1.25V ~ 36V DC (Adjustable) 5. Conversion Efficiency: Up to 96% 6. Input Voltage: 4.0V ~ 38V DC

blocks.text: The XL4015 Step Down Buck Converter is a DC-DC converter module built around the XL4015 chip, stepping down an input of 4.0V–38V DC to a continuously adjustable output between 1.25V and 36V DC. The input must be held at least 1.5V above the target output for correct regulation.

It delivers up to 5A of output current (a heatsink is recommended for continuous draw above 3A) and up to 75W of output power, with conversion efficiency reaching 96%. Onboard components include two 220µF 50V filter capacitors and a high-power toroidal inductor for stable output under load.

A 3-digit LED voltmeter display shows either input or output voltage via a tactile toggle button, while a multi-turn potentiometer allows fine-grained voltage adjustment. Screw terminal blocks handle both input and output connections.
Output current up to 5A, 75W max power
Multi-turn potentiometer for precise voltage setting
Screw terminal blocks for input and output
Suited for variable power supplies and high-power LED driving

name: LM2596 Step Down Buck Converter with Digital Display
desc: LM2596 Step Down Buck Converter with Digital Display 1. Main Chip: LM2596S 2. Output Current: 2A Rated (Up to 3A Max) 3. Output Power: 15W (Max, no heatsink) 4. Output Voltage: 1.25V ~ 37V DC (Adjustable) 5. Switching Frequency: 150 KHz 6. Input Voltage: 4.0V ~ 40V DC

blocks.text: The LM2596 Step Down Buck Converter is a DC-DC converter module built around the LM2596S chip, switching at 150 KHz to step down an input of 4.0V–40V DC to a continuously adjustable output between 1.25V and 37V DC. The input must stay at least 1.5V above the target output for correct regulation.

Rated output current is 2A continuous, with a maximum of 3A when a heatsink is fitted, delivering up to 15W without additional cooling. Conversion efficiency reaches up to 92%. Onboard filtering comes from a 220µF 35V capacitor plus a 100µF 50V capacitor, paired with a 470 SMD inductor.

A 3-digit LED voltmeter display toggles between input and output voltage via a tactile push button, while a multi-turn potentiometer allows fine voltage adjustment. Screw terminal blocks connect both input and output sides.
Output current: 2A rated, up to 3A with heatsink
Multi-turn potentiometer for precise voltage setting
Suited for battery charging and stepping down 12V/24V systems

blocks.text: This Waterproof USB Type-C Female Socket Connector is a 2-pin power-only connector — carrying VBUS and GND only, with no data lines — designed for panel-mounted power input applications rather than data transfer.

It comes with a 10cm wire pigtail pre-attached: red for VBUS (positive) and black for GND (negative), so it can be wired directly into a project without needing to solder onto the connector’s tiny internal pins.

The round panel-mount housing is built from durable plastic/PVC with a potted rear section for water resistance, making it suitable for outdoor and splash-exposed enclosures. It’s rated for typically 5V DC at up to 3A, and is available in black or white housing.

name: DC 3-6V High Voltage Step-Up Booster Module
desc: DC 3-6V High Voltage Step up/Booster Module 1. Input Voltage: 3V ~ 6V DC 2. Input Current: 2A ~ 5A 3. High Voltage Output: Up to 400kV (Pulse DC) 4. Discharge Distance: 10mm ~ 20mm 5. Dimensions: 27.3mm x 19.6mm x 20.75mm

blocks.text: This DC 3–6V High Voltage Step-Up/Booster Module is a pulse generator that converts a low 3V–6V DC input into a high-voltage pulsed DC output, drawing 2A to 5A of input current to generate discharge arcs of up to 400kV.

Input wiring uses a thin red wire for positive and a thin green wire for negative, while the high-voltage output is carried on thick translucent wires designed for arc discharge. At full output, the discharge distance is typically 10mm to 20mm.
The compact module measures 27.3mm x 19.6mm x 20.75mm and is fully epoxy resin potted, which provides insulation and shock resistance around the internal high-voltage components.

Because this module generates a genuine high-voltage arc, test the discharge distance starting from short to long, and avoid running it continuously for more than a few seconds at a time to prevent damaging the internal coils.
Epoxy resin potted for insulation and shock resistance
Suited for DIY electronic lighters and spark gap experiments

blocks.text: This Neon Flexible LED Strip is a silicone-jacketed LED strip designed to mimic the diffused, continuous glow of traditional neon tubing while running on 12V DC. The silicone jacket is flexible and heat-resistant, letting the strip be bent and shaped for custom signage and edge lighting.

Inside, LEDs are packed at a density of 120 per meter, and the diffusing silicone spreads the light evenly across a 120°–180° illumination angle, avoiding the visible individual LED dots seen on standard uncovered strips.

name: A4 Toner Transfer Paper for PCB Making
desc: A4 PCB Paper 1. Sheet Size: A4 (210mm x 297mm) 2. Printing Compatibility: Laser Printer / Photocopier Only 3. Working Principle: Heat-Activated Toner Transfer 4. Application: PCB Prototyping / DIY Circuit Board Etching

blocks.text: A4 PCB Paper is a toner transfer paper sized to standard A4 (210mm x 297mm), used for the toner-transfer method of making DIY printed circuit boards. It’s designed to work exclusively with laser printers or photocopiers, since the process relies on melting toner rather than ink.

The paper carries a high-gloss, heat-resistant release layer on its surface. A circuit layout is printed onto this layer using a laser printer, then transferred to a copper-clad board by applying heat — typically via a clothes iron or laminator — which releases the toner from the paper and bonds it to the copper.
Once transferred, the toner acts as a resist during etching, protecting the underlying copper traces while the rest of the copper is dissolved away, leaving the finished circuit pattern.
Low-cost method for DIY PCB prototyping

name: JGA25-370 DC Gear Motor with Magnetic Linear Encoder 6V 170RPM
desc: The JGA25-370 (6V, 170RPM) is a premium, all-metal DC gear motor equipped with a rear-mounted magnetic quadrature encoder. Delivering reliable torque and precise rotational feedback, it is the ideal choice for closed-loop control systems, robotics odometry, smart cars, and precision automation projects.

blocks.text: The JGA25-370 DC Gear Motor with Magnetic Encoder bridges the gap between simple DC motors and complex stepper motors by offering high-torque continuous rotation with precise positional feedback. Built around a standard 370-size DC motor and a 25mm all-metal gearbox, this motor operates at a nominal 6V to deliver a smooth 170 RPM at the output shaft.

What sets this motor apart is its integrated dual-channel Hall-effect magnetic encoder. By reading the quadrature pulse outputs (Channel A and Channel B), microcontrollers like Arduino, ESP32, or Raspberry Pi can calculate the motor’s exact speed, direction of rotation, and distance traveled. This makes it a perfect component for balancing robots, precise maze-solvers, PID speed controllers, and advanced automated machinery where blind rotation is not enough.
Closed-Loop Control Ready: The built-in magnetic Hall-effect encoder allows for precise speed tracking (RPM), position monitoring, and rotational direction sensing.
All-Metal Gearbox: Highly durable internal metal gears ensure a long lifespan, reduced wear, and the ability to handle stalls and high-torque loads better than plastic counterparts.
Standard D-Shaft: Features a 4mm D-shaped output shaft, ensuring a slip-free connection with a wide variety of wheels, pulleys, and shaft couplers.
Compact & Powerful: The 25mm diameter profile makes it easy to mount in tight chassis spaces while still delivering substantial pushing power for medium-sized robots.
6-Pin Interface: Comes with a neat 6-pin wiring terminal separating motor power from encoder logic, ensuring clean signals and safe microcontroller integration.

blocks.text: This Stepper Motor Cable is an adapter cable that converts a stepper motor’s 6-pin JST-PH connector into a 4-pin Dupont connector suited for driver boards, letting standard NEMA 17 stepper motors connect to drivers expecting a 4-wire bipolar input.

Connector A, on the motor side, is a 6-pin JST-PH connector (2.0mm pitch), while Connector B, on the driver side, is a 4-pin Dupont connector (2.54mm pitch) — matching the pin spacing used by most stepper driver headers.

name: Temperature Control Switch Module W1209
desc: The W1209 is a highly versatile, incredibly compact, and cost-effective 12V digital temperature controller module. Featuring a 3-digit LED display, onboard microcontroller, and an included waterproof NTC sensor, it is the perfect solution for DIY incubation, cooling systems, smart home automation, and custom thermal regulation projects.

blocks.text: The W1209 Temperature Control Switch Module delivers precise thermal management in an ultra-compact footprint. Designed for both hobbyists and industrial prototypers, this module allows you to intelligently control power to most types of electrical devices based on the temperature sensed by the included high-accuracy NTC temperature probe.

Despite its small size and low cost, the W1209 operates with an onboard microcontroller (MCU), meaning no advanced programming is required to get started. It features a simple three-button interface (SET, +, -) to configure the trigger temperatures and access a menu of seven hidden parameters (P0–P6), allowing users to adjust heating/cooling modes, hysteresis, upper/lower limits, and calibration. The onboard relay can handle loads up to 10A, making it highly capable of driving fans, heaters, peltier coolers, and other high-draw components.
Dual Operating Modes: Easily switch between Heating (triggers relay when temperature drops) and Cooling (triggers relay when temperature rises) modes.
High-Precision Sensing: Comes equipped with a waterproof NTC (10K 0.5%) sensor on a 50cm cable, allowing for safe liquid or enclosed-space temperature monitoring.
Onboard Memory: Retains your programmed settings and threshold values even after power loss.
Clear Visual Feedback: The bright 3-digit, 7-segment LED display provides real-time temperature readings alongside an onboard LED indicator that lights up when the relay is actively closed.
Industrial Build Quality: Features 100% machine patch components and wave soldering for stable, long-term performance.

desc: Protects against overvoltage and undervoltage Adjustable voltage limits for flexible protection Automatic power cutoff during abnormal conditions Auto-reconnect when voltage returns to normal Adjustable reconnection delay Digital LED display for real-time monitoring High accuracy voltage detection DIN rail design for easy installation

blocks.text: The Adjustable Voltage Protection Relay is a smart protection device designed to safeguard electrical appliances and equipment from abnormal voltage conditions. It automatically disconnects the power supply when the voltage exceeds or drops below the preset limits, preventing damage caused by overvoltage or undervoltage.

This protector continuously monitors the incoming power supply and restores the connection automatically once the voltage returns to the safe operating range. It is ideal for residential, commercial, and industrial applications where stable voltage is critical.
Over Voltage Protection: Automatically disconnects the load when voltage rises above the set limit.
Under Voltage Protection: Cuts off power when voltage falls below the safe threshold.
Adjustable Voltage Limits: User can set upper and lower voltage protection values.
Adjustable Reconnection Delay: Prevents frequent switching by adding a delay before reconnecting.
Digital LED Display: Shows real-time voltage values and device status.
High Accuracy Monitoring: Provides precise voltage measurement.
Automatic Recovery: Restores power once voltage returns to normal conditions.
DIN Rail Mount Design: Easy installation in electrical distribution boards.

The device constantly measures the incoming voltage from the power supply. If the voltage goes beyond the preset upper or lower limit, the internal relay disconnects the load immediately. After the voltage returns to the normal range and the preset delay time expires, the device reconnects the power automatically.
The protector is installed between the main circuit breaker (MCB) and the load. It is designed for DIN rail mounting, making it suitable for installation inside electrical distribution panels.

blocks.text: Bring your digital interfaces to life with the MAX7219 8×8 Dot Matrix LED Display Module. Built around the highly efficient MAX7219 serial input/output common-cathode display driver, this module allows you to control 64 individual red LEDs using only three digital pins on your microcontroller. The integrated chip automatically handles all multiplexing, decoding, and refresh rates. Furthermore, these modules are designed to be easily daisy-chained together, allowing you to build expansive scrolling text signs or custom data readouts with minimal wiring.
Efficient SPI-Compatible Interface: Requires only 3 I/O pins (DIN, CS, CLK) to control the entire 8×8 grid, drastically saving your microcontroller’s hardware resources.
Seamless Cascading: Features dedicated input and output header pins, allowing multiple matrix blocks to be daisy-chained together to create larger displays or scrolling tickers.
Integrated Hardware Driver: The onboard MAX7219 chip completely offloads LED multiplexing and current sourcing, ensuring a crisp, flicker-free display without taxing your main processor.
Software-Adjustable Brightness: The display intensity can be easily controlled programmatically via your microcontroller code to suit various ambient lighting conditions.
Plug-and-Play Prototyping: Comes equipped with standard 2.54mm header pins, making it immediately ready for breadboard insertion or standard Dupont jumper wire connections.

blocks.text: he 3S 20A 18650 Lithium Battery Charger Protection Module (BMS) is a high-performance battery management system designed for safe and efficient operation of 3-series lithium-ion battery packs. This module protects your batteries from overcharge, over-discharge, overcurrent, and short circuits—extending battery life while maintaining optimal performance.

Capable of handling up to 20A of continuous discharge current, this BMS is suitable for moderate to high-power applications, including e-bikes, power banks, DIY solar energy storage systems, portable electronics, and robotics. The board automatically balances the cells during charging, helping to maintain uniform voltage across all 3 cells and prevent capacity loss over time.

With built-in precision ICs and MOSFETs, the module delivers stable performance under various load conditions. Its compact form factor and easy-to-solder terminals make it ideal for DIYers and professional developers alike.
Designed for 3S (3 cells in series) lithium-ion or LiPo battery configurations, it supports 12.6V charging systems and works with 18650 and other compatible lithium battery types.

B+ → Connect to battery pack positive terminal
B- → Connect to battery pack negative terminal

Note: Use thick wires for high current paths. Always connect batteries before applying any charging or load.
Ensure battery cells are matched in voltage, capacity, and type before connecting.

blocks.text: Accurately measure ultraviolet radiation for your next environmental or wearable project with the GUVA-S12SD UV Light Sensor Module. Onboard Amplification: Features an integrated operational amplifier to stabilize and boost the sensor’s microvolt output to a usable, reliable level.

desc: Based on VL53L0X Time-of-Flight distance sensor Laser ranging up to 2 meters (light-dependent) High accuracy & precision — independent of surface reflectivity Supports Serial, PWM , and I2C communication Input voltage: 5V (with 2.8V regulator + level shifter) Built-in IR emitter + range sensor in a compact board Ideal for gesture sensing, obstacle avoidance, robotics Detachable mini PCB for 2.8V low-power applications

blocks.text: GY-53 VL53L0X Laser ToF Flight Time Ranging Sensor Module can be used for easy integration into your devices and basic gesture detection applications. Thanks to its 2.8V regulator and level shifters, the VL53L0X satellite board can be used in any application with a 2.8 to 5V supply.

The VL53L0X is a Time of Flight distance sensor like no other you’ve used! The sensor contains a very tiny invisible laser source and a matching sensor. The VL53L0X can detect the “time of flight”, or how long the light has taken to bounce back to the sensor. Since it uses a very narrow light source, it is good for determining the distance of only the surface directly in front of it.

Unlike sonars that bounce ultrasonic waves, the ‘cone’ of sense is very narrow. Unlike IR distance sensors that try to measure the amount of light bounced, the VL53L0x is much more precise and doesn’t have linearity problems or ‘double imaging’ where you can’t tell if an object is very far or very close.

The PCB section supporting the VL53L0X module is perforated so that developers can break off the mini PCB for use in a 2.8V supply application using flying leads. This makes it easier to integrate into development and evaluation devices due to its small form factor.

The module is designed for low-power operation. Ranging measurements can be automatically performed at user-defined intervals. Multiple thresholds and interrupt schemes are supported to minimize host operations. Serial port and PWM to read the data code: STM32, Arduino, 51 MCU.

Note that due to the infrared will be affected by the outside light, in the light will affect the maximum range of measurement, will not affect the measurement accuracy. Default configuration: serial baud rate 9600, automatic output, high precision mode. When using, please remove the sensor film.

The VL53L0X is the latest product based on ST’s patented FlightSense™ technology. This is a ground-breaking technology allowing absolute distance to be measured independent of target reflectance. Instead of estimating the distance by measuring the amount of light reflected back from the object (which is significantly influenced by color and surface), the VL53L0X precisely measures the time the light takes to travel to the nearest object and reflect back to the sensor (Time-of-Flight). Combining an IR emitter and a range sensor, the VL53L0X is easy to integrate and saves OEMs long and costly optical and mechanical design optimizations.

Note: The VL53L0X is delivered with a liner, in order to prevent potential foreign material to penetrate inside the modules holes during the assembly process. It must be removed at the latest possible step during final assembly, and anyway before module calibration.

blocks.text: This 10 x 10 cm single-sided copper clad board is a blank FR2 (phenolic paper) PCB laminate for making your own printed circuit boards. One side is covered with bare copper, ready for toner transfer and etching, photo-resist or CNC milling, so you can turn a circuit design into a real, neat board at home, in the lab or at school.
Layers: single-sided (copper on one side only)
Clean the copper with fine sandpaper or steel wool, then wipe it with alcohol until it is bright.
Print the mirrored layout on glossy paper with a laser printer and iron it onto the copper.
Soak the board in water, peel the paper off and touch up any missing tracks with a permanent marker.
Etch in ferric chloride until the uncovered copper is gone, then rinse with water.
Remove the toner with acetone, drill the holes (0.8 to 1mm suits most components) and solder.
Ferric chloride is corrosive and stains: wear gloves and eye protection, work in a ventilated place and do not pour used etchant down the drain.
Wear a mask when cutting, sanding or drilling the board, as the dust irritates the lungs and skin.
Cut the board with a hacksaw, or score both sides deeply along a ruler and snap it.

desc: Based on ATmega328 microcontroller FT232 USB-to-Serial driver for stable PC communication Compact and breadboard-friendly design 22 total I/O pins (14 Digital, 8 Analog) Supports serial, I2C, and SPI communication Onboard voltage regulator (5V & 3.3V) Preloaded with Arduino bootloader for easy programming Ideal for IoT, robotics, sensors, and embedded systems

blocks.text: The Arduino Nano 3.0 Controller Board with an FT232 USB-to-Serial chip is a compact and powerful microcontroller board that is widely used in DIY electronics projects, prototyping, and embedded systems. It offers most of the functionality of the Arduino Uno but in a much smaller form factor. The FT232 chip is an essential part of this version, as it is responsible for handling communication between the Arduino and your computer over USB.
Key Features of Arduino Nano 3.0 with FT232

The Arduino Nano 3.0 is based on the ATmega328P microcontroller, which is the same chip used in the Arduino Uno. It offers 32KB of flash memory (of which 2KB is used by the bootloader), 2KB of SRAM, and 1KB of EEPROM.

The FT232 chip on the board acts as the USB-to-Serial interface, allowing the board to communicate with your computer. It converts the USB data from your computer into the appropriate serial communication protocol (UART) for the ATmega328P microcontroller. This chip enables easy uploading of code via USB without needing a separate USB-to-serial adapter.

One of the standout features of the Arduino Nano is its small form factor. It is ideal for projects where space is limited and is often used in wearable electronics, small robots, or compact sensor applications.
The Arduino Nano provides 14 digital I/O pins, of which 6 can be used as PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) outputs.
Analog Input Pins: It has 8 analog input pins (A0 to A7) for reading analog sensors, such as temperature sensors, light sensors, or potentiometers.
1 UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) is available for serial communication. This is essential for debugging, sending data to/from the board, and interfacing with other serial devices.
The Arduino Nano can be powered either through the USB connection or via the Vin pin, which can accept voltages between 6V and 12V.
It has a 5V regulator to supply the board and attached peripherals with 5V power.
The board operates at a clock speed of 16 MHz, providing enough processing power for a wide range of applications.
The board comes with a pre-installed bootloader, so you can easily upload code via USB without needing a separate programmer. The FT232 USB-to-serial chip facilitates this process.

blocks.text: The FT232 USB-to-Serial chip provides an interface between the Arduino Nano and your computer. This chip is responsible for the following functions:
Serial communication: It enables data exchange between the computer and the Arduino Nano through the USB cable. This is used for uploading sketches, serial communication, and debugging.

Driver Support: The FT232 requires a driver (typically installed automatically) to enable proper USB functionality. This driver is compatible with Windows, macOS, and Linux, and ensures reliable communication between the microcontroller and your development environment (e.g., Arduino IDE).
How to Use the Arduino Nano 3.0 with FT232

Depending on your operating system, you may need to install the FTDI drivers for the FT232 chip. The Arduino IDE generally includes the necessary drivers, but sometimes you may need to download them separately from the FTDI website.
Connect the Nano to Your Computer:
Plug the USB cable into the Arduino Nano and connect it to your computer. The FT232 chip will manage the USB-to-serial communication.
Select the Board and Port in Arduino IDE:
Go to Tools > Board > Arduino Nano.
Under Tools > Port, select the correct serial port (it will typically be labeled as a COM port on Windows or /dev/ttyUSB on Linux/macOS).
Write your Arduino code (called a “sketch”) in the IDE and click the Upload button.
The FT232 chip will handle the communication between the Arduino IDE and the microcontroller, allowing your sketch to be uploaded over the USB connection.
Here is a simple example of blinking an LED using the Arduino Nano:
This code will blink the LED connected to pin 13 on the Arduino Nano every second.
Advantages of Using Arduino Nano 3.0 with FT232
Compact Size: The Arduino Nano is ideal for projects where space is limited.
Easy USB Programming: With the FT232 chip, uploading code via USB is simple and doesn’t require additional hardware like a separate USB-to-serial adapter.
Low Cost: The Arduino Nano is one of the most affordable Arduino boards, making it ideal for prototyping and educational projects.
Wide Compatibility: It’s fully compatible with the Arduino IDE, which provides a wide variety of libraries and examples to help you get started quickly.
Wearable Devices: Due to its small size, the Arduino Nano is ideal for wearable electronics such as heart rate monitors, fitness trackers, or medical monitoring devices.
Robotics: Its compact size and sufficient processing power make the Arduino Nano a great choice for small robots or automated systems.
Sensor Networks: It’s commonly used in environmental monitoring, home automation, and IoT projects, especially when you need to interface with multiple sensors.
Prototyping: Many hobbyists and engineers use the Arduino Nano to prototype electronic circuits and systems in a compact form.

The Arduino Nano 3.0 with the FT232 USB-to-serial chip is a versatile and compact microcontroller board that allows you to easily prototype electronics projects. Its small size, USB interface, and compatibility with the Arduino IDE make it a great choice for a wide range of applications, from wearables to robotics and beyond. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced maker, the Arduino Nano is a powerful tool for creating innovative projects.

blocks.text: The 100nF (0.1µF) 50V ceramic capacitor, marked “104”, is the most common decoupling capacitor in electronics. Placed right next to the power pins of an IC, microcontroller or sensor module, it absorbs fast voltage spikes and noise on the supply line and keeps the circuit stable. Every electronics kit and repair bench needs a supply of them.
Decoupling: connect one leg to the IC’s VCC pin and the other to GND, as close to the pins as possible.
No polarity: it can be fitted either way round.
With an electrolytic: pair it with a larger electrolytic capacitor (for example 100µF) on a power rail; the electrolytic handles slow ripple and the 100nF handles fast noise.

Noise suppression across the terminals of small DC motors
Button debouncing: with a 10K Ohm pull-up, the time constant is 10KΩ × 100nF = 1 ms
Input and output capacitors for voltage regulators such as the 7805
Keep the leads short; long leads reduce the filtering effect at high frequencies.

blocks.text: A 12V 40W heater is a type of electric heater designed to operate at 12 volts DC and consume 40 watts of power. These heaters are commonly used in various applications, including in automotive, DIY projects, small portable heating devices, and even in some hobby electronics for temperature regulation or warming purposes.
Key Specifications and Features of a 12V 40W Heater
This is the voltage required to operate the heater. It is commonly used in systems powered by car batteries, solar panels, or DC power supplies.
The heater consumes 40 watts of power when in operation. This will determine how much current it draws from the 12V source.

To calculate the current draw of a 12V 40W heater, we use Ohm’s law: I=PV=40W12V=3.33AI = frac{P}{V} = frac{40W}{12V} = 3.33AI=VP​=12V40W​=3.33A So, the heater will draw approximately 3.33 amps of current at full power.
The heater typically consists of a resistive heating element (often made of metal wire, like nichrome), which heats up when electrical current passes through it.
Automotive: 12V heaters are commonly used in cars, trucks, or RVs for defrosting windows or as personal cabin heaters.
DIY Projects: 12V heaters can be used in custom heating solutions, such as incubators, soldering stations, or small space heaters.
Portable Devices: Small portable heating devices for camping, boating, or in applications where a 12V power supply is used, such as in some recreational vehicles (RVs).
Aquarium Heaters: In small fish tanks or reptile enclosures, where low-voltage heaters are needed.
12V 40W heaters can be relatively compact and efficient for small heating tasks. However, they will not be suitable for large-scale heating applications as they are low-power devices.
The physical design varies, but they are typically either a ceramic-based heating element, a metal coil surrounded by insulation, or carbon fiber heaters.
Overcurrent Protection: Given the current draw of 3.33A, it’s important to ensure that the power supply or wiring can handle this without overheating.
Temperature Control: It’s recommended to include a temperature sensor or thermostat in the circuit to avoid overheating, especially if the heater is used in an enclosed space.
Since the heater operates at 12V DC, it will need a power source that can supply at least 3.33 amps at 12V. Common options include:
12V DC power supplies: These are typically used for stationary applications, like powering the heater from a wall outlet (AC to DC).
12V battery: Used in mobile or off-grid applications, such as with solar panels, or in vehicles like cars, RVs, or boats.
Make sure to connect the positive terminal of your 12V power supply to the positive terminal of the heater and the negative terminal to the negative terminal.
Use wires capable of handling the 3.33A current without excessive heating. For example, 18 AWG wire should be suitable for most cases.
Once connected, when you apply power to the heater, the resistive element will begin to heat up, converting the electrical energy into heat.
To control the temperature of the heater, you can add a thermostat or PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) control, which can modulate the heater’s power and prevent overheating.
Since the heater will generate heat, ensure the surrounding area has adequate ventilation to prevent heat buildup, which could lead to component failure or fire hazards.
12V Power Supply (capable of delivering at least 3.33A)
Thermostat or Temperature Sensor (optional, for automatic control)
Connect the positive terminal of the 12V power supply to the positive terminal of the heater.
Connect the negative terminal of the heater to the negative terminal of the power supply.
Optionally, wire a thermostat or temperature sensor in series with the heater to control the on/off state of the heater based on the temperature.
Place a 4A fuse in series with the positive power line to protect the heater from potential overcurrent situations.

Heating Rate: The heater will provide 40 watts of thermal energy when fully powered. The efficiency of heat transfer depends on the material and how well it is insulated. For a small space, this could be sufficient to raise the temperature to a comfortable level.

Energy Usage: At full load, the heater will consume 40 watts per hour (Wh), or 0.04 kWh. If used for several hours, this can add up, so be mindful of energy consumption if using batteries or solar power.

blocks.text: The 74LS195 is a high-speed 4-Bit Universal Shift Register offering typical shift frequencies of 39 MHz. It is useful for a wide variety of registers and counting applications. It utilizes the Schottky diode clamped process to achieve high speeds and is fully compatible with all Motorola TTL products. The 74LS195 IC output always comes in TTL which makes it easy to work with other TTL devices and microcontrollers. The IC 74LS195 is smaller in size and it has a much faster speed which makes it reliable in every kind of device.
What is a Universal Shift Register?

Universal Shift registers are an integral part of digital memory circuitry usually found in devices such as calculators, computers, and data processing systems. With a universal shift register, data or bits can be entered into the system in a serial or parallel manner. Data entry using 74LS195 is usually done from one direction, and as more data is added, it shifts positions until the data gets to the output end. The two ends are referred to as the left and right end. The movement of data can be from left to right, from right to left, or in both directions to make a bidirectional shift register.

blocks.text: This 20kg load cell is a strain-gauge weight sensor in a full Wheatstone bridge, made for building digital scales and force measurement projects. Its output is a very small voltage that changes with the applied weight, so it is normally connected to an HX711 24-bit amplifier module and read by an Arduino, ESP32 or ESP8266.
At 5V excitation the full-scale signal is only about 5 mV (5V × 1 mV/V), which is why an amplifier like the HX711 is needed.

Using the common HX711 library: scale.begin(DT_PIN, SCK_PIN); scale.set_scale(calibration_factor); scale.tare(); then read the weight with scale.get_units(10). Find the calibration factor once by placing a known weight on the cell.

blocks.text: The MAX9814 Microphone Amplifier Module with Auto-Gain Control (AGC) is a popular audio amplification module for use with microcontrollers like Arduino. It’s designed to amplify audio signals from a microphone while automatically adjusting the gain to ensure consistent output levels, even when the input signal varies in volume. This feature makes it especially useful for applications where the input sound may vary, such as voice recognition, audio sensing, or other sound-related projects.

The MAX9814 automatically adjusts the microphone’s gain based on the input signal’s strength. If the sound is quiet, the amplifier boosts the signal; if the sound is loud, the amplifier reduces its gain to avoid distortion.
The module has an integrated electret microphone, which converts sound into an analog electrical signal.
Designed with a low-noise preamp, the module provides clean amplification of audio signals.
Although the AGC does most of the work, there is an option to manually adjust the gain using a potentiometer if desired.
The module outputs an analog signal that can be fed directly into an analog input pin on an Arduino or other microcontroller.
It typically operates on a voltage range of 2.7V to 5.5V, making it compatible with most microcontrollers, including Arduino boards running on 5V or 3.3V.
The module typically has the following pins:
GAIN: Optional pin for external gain control (some versions include a potentiometer or jumper for manual gain adjustment)
VCC connects to the 5V (or 3.3V, depending on your module) pin on the Arduino.
GND connects to the GND pin on the Arduino.
OUT connects to one of the analog input pins on the Arduino, like A0.

The analogRead() function reads the analog signal from the microphone output. The value will vary based on the sound pressure level (volume) captured by the microphone.
The Arduino can process the data from the microphone to detect sound events, measure the sound intensity, or even use it for speech recognition or sound-activated systems.
Sound-activated lights or devices: For example, turning on an LED or triggering an action when a certain sound level is detected.
Voice recognition systems: Capturing audio input for voice-activated systems.
Sound level monitoring: Detecting ambient noise levels for applications like smart homes or noise-sensitive environments.
Audio projects: Amplifying sound for audio input in a variety of projects.
The output of the MAX9814 will be an analog signal, and the Arduino’s ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter) will convert this signal into a digital value (range from 0 to 1023).
To get the best results, keep the microphone module’s microphone within a reasonable distance from the sound source.
Depending on your application, you might want to apply filters or smoothing techniques to the raw data to reduce noise or fluctuations in the reading.
By using the MAX9814 with AGC, you can create more consistent sound-based interactions with Arduino, even in environments with variable background noise.

blocks.text: The GY-271 HMC5883L Triple-Axis Magnetometer Sensor Module is a popular sensor used to measure the magnetic field in three dimensions (X, Y, and Z axes). It uses the HMC5883L magnetometer IC, which is designed for accurate and low-power magnetic field sensing, and is widely used in various applications like electronic compasses, robotics, and other systems where orientation and navigation are important.
Key Features of GY-271 HMC5883L Module
The sensor can measure the magnetic field along the X, Y, and Z axes, making it ideal for detecting the orientation and direction of the sensor relative to Earth’s magnetic field.

The HMC5883L has a configurable sensitivity range of ±0.88 Gauss to ±8.1 Gauss, which determines how sensitive the sensor is to the Earth’s magnetic field. The default range is typically set to ±1.3 Gauss for most applications, providing good resolution for compass or heading applications.

The HMC5883L communicates with a microcontroller (like Arduino) using the I2C protocol. This makes it easy to connect and interact with microcontrollers, as only two wires (SCL and SDA) are needed for communication, in addition to power and ground.

The module operates with low power, making it suitable for battery-powered applications. It’s typically used in systems where power consumption is a concern, such as portable devices and mobile robotics.
The GY-271 module is small and easy to integrate into various projects. Its compact size makes it ideal for portable devices and systems with limited space.
The GY-271 module typically includes an onboard voltage regulator, so it can be powered by a range of voltages (usually 3.3V to 5V).

blocks.text: This is AS608 Optical Fingerprint Sensor Fingerprint Module.

The fingerprint algorithm extracts features from the acquired fingerprint image and represents the fingerprint information. The storage, comparison, and search of fingerprints are all done by operating fingerprint features.

Fingerprint processing includes two processes: fingerprint registration process and fingerprint matching process (in which fingerprint matching is divided into fingerprint comparison (1:1) and fingerprint search (1:N) two ways).
When the fingerprint is registered, two fingerprints are entered for each fingerprint, and the input image is processed twice. The synthesis module is stored in the module.

When the fingerprint is matched, the fingerprint sensor is used to input the fingerprint image to be verified and processed, and then it is compared with the fingerprint module in the module (if it is matched with a module specified in the module, it is called fingerprint comparison mode, ie, 1:1 mode. If matching with multiple modules is called fingerprint search, ie 1:N mode, the module gives the matching result (pass or fail).

blocks.text: This is a simple but very useful module which uses a potential divider to reduce an input voltage by a factor of 5. The Voltage Detection Sensor Module 25V allows you to use the analog input of a microcontroller to monitor voltages much higher than it capable of sensing.
For example with a 0-5V analog input range, you are able to measure a voltage up to 25V. This voltage sensor module also includes convenient screw terminals for easy and secure connection of a wire.

This module is based on the principle of resistive voltage divider design, can make the red terminal connector input voltage to 5 times smaller. Arduino analog input voltages up to 5 v, the voltage detection module input voltage not greater than 5Vx5=25V (if using 3.3V systems, input voltage not greater than 3.3Vx5=16.5V).
Arduino AVR chips have 10-bit AD, so this module simulates a resolution of 0.00489V (5V/1023), so the minimum voltage of input voltage detection module is 0.00489Vx5=0.02445V.
Keep in mind, you are restricted to voltages that are less than 25 volts. More than that and you will exceed the voltage limit of your Arduino input.

OLED (Organic Light-Emitting Diode) is a self-light-emitting technology composed of a thin, multi-layered organic film placed between an anode and cathode. In contrast to LCD technology, OLED does not require a backlight. OLED possesses high application potential for virtually all types of displays and is regarded as the ultimate technology for the next generation of flat-panel displays.

OLEDs basic structure consists of organic materials positioned between the cathode and the anode, which is composed of electric conductive transparent Indium Tin Oxide (ITO). The organic materials compose a multi-layered thin film, which includes the Hole Transporting Layer (HTL), Emission Layer (EML) and the Electron Transporting Layer (ETL). By applying the appropriate electric voltage, holes and electrons are injected into the EML from the anode and the cathode, respectively. The holes and electrons combine inside the EML to form excitons, after which electroluminescence occurs. The transfer material, emission layer material, and choice of electrode are the key factors that determine the quality of OLED components.

blocks.text: Dark Light Circuit Kit PCB Board Description

This DIY Dark Light Circuit Kit PCB Board is perfect for electronics enthusiasts and hobbyists looking to create a practical and educational project. The kit includes all the necessary components to assemble a functional dark light sensor circuit, allowing an LED to light up when it gets dark. Here’s what’s included and how it works:
PCB Board: High-quality printed circuit board designed to neatly and securely hold all components.
LDR (Light Dependent Resistor): Senses the ambient light levels. The resistance of the LDR changes with the light intensity.
Potentiometer (100K): Allows you to adjust the sensitivity of the circuit to the ambient light.
BC547 Transistor: Acts as a switch, turning on the LED when the light level drops below a certain threshold.
LED: Lights up when it gets dark, providing a visual indication.
Additional Components: Resistors, capacitors, and connectors necessary for the circuit.
Educational DIY Kit: Perfect for learning about basic electronics, transistors, and light-dependent circuits.
Easy Assembly: Clear PCB layout with labeled components for straightforward soldering.
Adjustable Sensitivity: Fine-tune the circuit’s response to light using the potentiometer.
Compact Design: Fits into various DIY projects, from simple educational setups to more complex light-activated systems.
Light Sensing: The LDR detects the ambient light level. As it gets darker, the resistance of the LDR increases.
Sensitivity Adjustment: The potentiometer (100K) adjusts the threshold at which the LED will turn on.
Transistor Switching: When the light level drops below the set threshold, the BC547 transistor switches on, allowing current to flow through the LED.
LED Illumination: The LED lights up, indicating that the circuit has detected low light conditions.

This Dark Light Circuit Kit is an excellent way to delve into the world of electronics, offering hands-on experience and practical application. Whether you’re a beginner or an experienced hobbyist, this kit provides a fun and educational project.

desc: Operating voltage: 5V Provide both digital and analog output Adjustable sensitivity Output LED indicator Compatible with Arduino TTL Compatible Bolt holes for easy installation

blocks.text: The Raindrops Detection sensor module is used for rain detection. It is also for measuring rainfall intensity. Rain sensor can be used for all kinds of weather monitoring and translated into output signals and AO.

Raindrops Detection Sensor Module Rain Weather Module for Arduino, etc. Rain sensor can be used to monitor a variety of weather conditions and turned into several fixed output signal and Analog output.

It includes a printed circuit board (control board) that “collects” the raindrops. As raindrops are collected on the circuit board, they create paths of parallel resistance that are measured via the op-amp. The lower the resistance (or the more water), the lower the voltage output. Conversely, the less water, the greater the output voltage on the analog pin. A completely dry board, for example, will cause the module to output 5V.

The module includes a rain board and a control board that is separate for more convenience. It has a power indicator LED and an adjustable sensitivity through a potentiometer. The module is based on the LM393 op-amp.

blocks.text: This is Industrial Grade Analog PH Sensor Kit. Need to measure water quality and other parameters but haven’t got any low-cost pH meter? Find it difficult to use with Arduino?
Here, we have an Industrial Grade Analog PH Sensor Kit. This probe can be used with this pH sensor module.

The Analog pH Sensor Kit is specially designed for Arduino controllers and has a built-in simple, convenient, and practical connection and features. It has an LED that works as the Power Indicator, a BNC connector, and a PH2.0 sensor interface. To use it, just connect the pH sensor with the BND connector, and plug the PH2.0 interface into the analog input port of any Arduino controller. If pre-programmed, you will get the pH value easily. Comes in a compact plastic box with foams for better mobile storage
Note: This is a laboratory probe, it can’t be immersed in the liquid for a too long time.
To Explore More pH Sensors, Click here
#define SensorPin A0 // the pH meter Analog output is connected with the Arduino’s Analog
unsigned long int avgValue; //Store the average value of the sensor feedback
for(int i=0;i<10;i++) //Get 10 sample value from the sensor for smooth the value
for(int i=0;i<9;i++) //sort the analog from small to large
for(int i=2;i<8;i++) //take the average value of 6 center sample
float phValue=(float)avgValue*5.0/1024/6; //convert the analog into millivolt
phValue=3.5*phValue; //convert the millivolt into pH value
Step to Use the pH Meter
Please use an external switching power supply, and the voltage as close as possible to the +5.00V. More accurate the voltage, the higher the accuracy!

Before the electrode is continuously used every time, you need to calibrate it by the standard solution, in order to obtain more accurate results. The best environment temperature is about 25 ℃, and the pH value is known and reliable, close to the measured value. If you measure the acidic sample, the pH value of the standard solution should be 4.00. If you measure the alkaline sample, the pH value of the standard solution should be 9.18.Subsection calibration, just in order to get better accuracy.
Before the pH electrode is measured in different solutions, we need to use water to wash it. We recommend using deionized water.

Connect equipment according to the graphic, that is, the pH electrode is connected to the BNC connector on the pH meter board，and then use the connection lines, the pH meter board is connected to the analog port 0 of the Arduino controller. When the Arduino controller gets power, you will see the blue LED on board is on.
Upload the sample code to the Arduino controller.

Put the pH electrode into the standard solution whose pH value is 7.00，or directly shorten the input of the BNC connector. Open the serial monitor of the Arduino IDE, you can see the pH value printed on it, and the error does not exceed 0.3. Record the pH value printed, then compared with 7.00, and the difference should be changed into the “Offset” in the sample code. For example, the pH value printed is 6.88, so the difference is 0.12. You should change the “# define Offset 0.00” into “# define Offset 0.12” in your program.

Put the pH electrode into the pH standard solution whose value is 4.00. Then wait about one minute, adjust the gain potential device, let the value stabilize at around 4.00. At this time, the acidic calibration has been completed and you can measure the pH value of an acidic solution.
Note: If you want to measure the pH value of other solutions, you must wash the pH electrode first!

blocks.text: The 74HC240 is an octal buffer/line driver IC, used to boost drive strength and isolate logic signals across two independent 4-bit sections, each with its own active-low output-enable control. This makes it useful for driving multiple downstream loads or long PCB traces from a microcontroller pin that can’t supply enough current on its own.

As a buffer/line driver rather than a latch or counter, it passes the logic state of its inputs through to its outputs (inverted, in the case of the 74240 family) without storing any state, making it purely a signal-conditioning component in a digital circuit.

DIP switches are often used in electronics for setting hardware configurations, such as device IDs, jumper settings, or enabling/disabling features.
