blocks.text: The CD4093 is a CMOS logic IC with four independent 2-input NAND gates whose inputs have Schmitt-trigger action. The built-in hysteresis turns slow, noisy or bouncing signals into clean, sharp logic levels, so a single chip can debounce switches, square up sensor signals and build simple oscillators with just one resistor and one capacitor. Its wide supply range and very low power make it ideal for battery projects.

Tie both inputs of one gate together, connect a resistor from the output back to the inputs, and a capacitor from the inputs to GND. The gate produces a square wave; a larger resistor or capacitor gives a lower frequency, and the exact value also depends on the supply voltage.

Place a 0.1µF capacitor between VDD and GND near the IC, and handle the chip with static precautions.

It is built using CMOS technology to achieve low power consumption, high noise immunity, and compatibility with a wide supply voltage range.
This device is ideal for digital systems requiring logic control, timing operations, and multi-condition gating.
Compatible with TTL input levels (at 5V VDD)

name: CD4070 Quad Exclusive-OR Gate
desc: CMOS Quad 2-Input Exclusive-OR (XOR) Gate Low power consumption, high noise immunity Works from 3V to 15V TTL-compatible logic levels Ideal for parity checking , logic operations , and digital control

blocks.text: The CD4070 is a CMOS logic integrated circuit that contains four independent 2-input Exclusive-OR (XOR) gates. Each gate outputs HIGH only when the inputs differ (i.e., one input HIGH, the other LOW). It is ideal for logic comparison, arithmetic logic, signal inversion, and parity generation.
Thanks to its low power consumption, high noise immunity, and wide supply voltage range, the CD4070 is widely used in digital systems and embedded electronics.
TTL compatible inputs and outputs (at VDD = 5V)

name: CD4066 Quad Bilateral Switch
desc: CD4066 Quad Bilateral Switch 1. Type: 4 independent bidirectional switches 2. On-Resistance: 100Ω typical at 10V 3. Supply Voltage: 3V to 15V DC 4. Logic Family: 40xx series CMOS 5. Package: 14-pin DIP

blocks.text: The CD4066 is a quad bilateral switch from the 40xx series CMOS logic family. This device contains four independent bidirectional switches, each capable of passing signals in either direction under logic control. Each switch is implemented as a CMOS transmission gate with independent enable input, providing a complete analog or digital switching solution in a single package.

The CD4066 is a major improvement over earlier switch devices, offering much lower on-resistance and improved linearity. These switches can handle both analog and digital signals across a wide voltage range. Typical applications include signal routing, audio switching, gain control circuits, and general-purpose analog switching in instrumentation and communication systems.
Low signal distortion and excellent linearity

name: CD4060 14-Stage Ripple-Carry Binary
desc: CD4060 14-Stage Ripple-Carry Binary Counter 1. Type: 14-stage binary counter with oscillator 2. Stages: 14 ripple-carry stages 3. Supply Voltage: 3V to 15V DC 4. Logic Family: 40xx series CMOS 5. Package: 16-pin DIP

blocks.text: The CD4060 is a 14-stage ripple-carry binary counter with an integrated oscillator, from the 40xx series CMOS logic family. This device combines a 14-stage binary counter with a built-in oscillator that can be externally configured with a resistor and capacitor or a crystal. The oscillator’s frequency is divided down by the counter stages, generating multiple frequency outputs at each stage.

The CD4060 is commonly used as a time-base generator, frequency divider, or timer in applications such as clock generation, long-duration timers, and low-frequency oscillators. Each of the 14 counter stages provides a divided output, allowing selection of various timing intervals. The device can also be used with an external clock input when not using the internal oscillator. A master reset input clears all stages to zero and disables the oscillator.
Built-in oscillator for RC or crystal operation

blocks.text: The CD4052 is a differential 4-channel analog multiplexer/demultiplexer IC, routing one of 4 differential (2-line) channels to a common differential output pair based on a 2-bit binary select code.

Being differential, it switches pairs of signal lines together rather than single lines, useful for routing balanced or differential analog signals such as stereo audio channels or differential sensor pairs.
Part of the CD40xx CMOS logic family, this IC is a standard building block for differential analog signal routing circuits.

blocks.text: The CD4047 is a monostable/astable multivibrator IC, capable of operating either as a one-shot timer (monostable mode) generating a single output pulse, or as a free-running oscillator (astable mode) generating a continuous square wave.

The timing period in either mode is set by an external RC (resistor-capacitor) network, letting the pulse width or oscillation frequency be tuned to the application without additional digital timing logic.
Part of the CD40xx CMOS logic family, this IC is a standard building block for pulse generation and oscillator circuits.
Timing set via external RC network

blocks.text: The CD4046 is a micropower phase-locked loop (PLL) IC, combining a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) and phase comparators on one chip to lock an internal oscillator’s frequency and phase to an external reference signal.

This PLL structure is a standard building block for frequency synthesis, FM demodulation, tone decoding, and clock recovery circuits, using its low-power CMOS design to keep current draw minimal in battery-powered applications.
Part of the CD40xx CMOS logic family, this IC is a standard building block for phase-locking and frequency synthesis circuits.
Low current draw, suited for battery-powered designs

As a ripple counter, each stage triggers the next in sequence, making it a simple, low-part-count way to implement long binary counting or frequency division chains.
Part of the CD40xx CMOS logic family, this IC is a standard building block for counting and frequency division circuits.
Divides input frequency by up to 4096

blocks.text: The CD4029 is a binary-decade up/down counter IC, selectable between binary (base-2) and decade (base-10) counting modes, counting either upward or downward depending on its control inputs.

This dual-mode flexibility lets a single IC serve either as a binary counter or a decimal (BCD) counter depending on how it’s configured, reducing the need for separate binary and decade counter ICs in mixed designs.
Part of the CD40xx CMOS logic family, this IC is a standard building block for flexible counting circuits.
Selectable binary or decade counting mode

The JK flip-flop configuration allows set, reset, toggle, and hold states depending on the J and K inputs, making it a versatile building block for counters, frequency dividers, and general sequential logic circuits.
Part of the CD40xx CMOS logic family, this IC is a standard building block for sequential logic circuits.

blocks.text: The CD4021 is an 8-stage static shift register IC, shifting serial data in bit-by-bit through 8 static storage stages, letting a single serial line be converted to 8 parallel output lines.

Being static, the register retains its data indefinitely as long as power is applied, without needing a refresh clock, useful for parallel-to-serial or serial-to-parallel conversion in low-speed data expansion applications.
Part of the CD40xx CMOS logic family, this IC is a standard building block for serial/parallel data conversion circuits.

Having four gates on one chip lets a single IC handle four separate 2-input NAND functions in a design, reducing part count compared to using single-gate packages — one of the most widely used basic logic gate ICs.

The CD4053 operates over a wide voltage range and is ideal for signal routing, analog multiplexing, audio switching, and low-voltage control systems.

For input codes 1010 to 1111, all outputs remain LOW, ensuring valid BCD decoding only.
This decoder is ideal for numeric display control, digital instrumentation, and other applications where binary-to-decimal conversion is needed.

0.33µF capacitor between Input and Ground, close to the regulator.
Use capacitors rated 50V, because the input can be above 35V.

A linear regulator turns the extra voltage into heat: P = (Vin − 24V) × I. For example, 30V in and 0.4A out gives (30 − 24) × 0.4 = 2.4W, which needs a heatsink. Keep the input only a few volts above 24V to reduce heat.
The L7824CV can only step voltage down. To get 24V from 12V, use a boost converter instead.

blocks.text: The resistance of 12mm GL12528 Light Sensitive Photoresistor LDR changes with the change in the ambient light exposed on the surface of the sensor. As the light on the sensor increases then the resistance across the two leads decreases. name: TIP127 PNP Darlington Transistor
desc: 🔌 TIP127 PNP Darlington power transistor 💪 High current gain—easy control with low base current ⚡ Ideal for switching motors, relays, solenoids, and lamps 🧩 Great for high-side switching with Arduino/MCUs 🛠️ TO-220 package—easy mounting and heatsinking 🔥 Use a heatsink for high current/continuous loads 🔁 Darlington design for strong amplification ✅ Reliable choice for power driver circuits

blocks.text: The TIP127 is a PNP Darlington power transistor in a TO-220 package, rated 100V and 5A, and the complementary partner of the TIP122. Its high current gain (at least 1000) makes it a simple choice for high-side switching, where the load stays connected to ground and the transistor switches the positive supply, and for push-pull and H-bridge stages together with the TIP122.
Power dissipation: 65W (case at 25°C, on a heatsink)
Emitter to the positive supply (for example 12V); load between the Collector and GND.

The transistor turns on when the Base is pulled down. An Arduino pin cannot switch it off on a 12V supply, so use a small NPN transistor (such as 2N2222 or BC547): Arduino pin through 1KΩ to the NPN base, NPN emitter to GND, NPN collector through 1KΩ to the TIP127 Base. Base current: (12V − 1.5V − 0.2V) ÷ 1KΩ ≈ 10 mA.
For an inductive load, add a 1N4007 diode across it, cathode to the Collector side.
On a 5V supply only, the Arduino pin can drive the Base directly through 1KΩ: LOW = on, HIGH = off.
With the NPN pre-driver on pin 7, HIGH turns the load on:
About 1 to 2V drops across the transistor when on, so use a heatsink above about 1A. The tab is the Collector: insulate it from other parts.

name: TIP122 Silicon NPN Power Darlington Transistor 5A 100V 65W
desc: 🔌 TIP122 silicon NPN power Darlington transistor 💪 Current rating: up to 5A ⚡ Voltage rating: 100V 🔥 Power dissipation: up to 65W (with proper heatsink) 🧩 Ideal for driving relays, motors, solenoids, and high-power LEDs 🔁 High gain Darlington pair—easy to drive from Arduino/MCU 🛠️ TO-220 package for easy mounting and cooling ✅ Great for low-side switching and power control circuits

blocks.text: The TIP122 is an NPN Darlington power transistor in a TO-220 package, rated 100V and 5A. Its very high current gain (at least 1000) lets a microcontroller pin switch motors, relays, solenoids, lamps and LED strips with only a few milliamps of base current. It is one of the most popular choices for simple low-side power switching with Arduino.
Power dissipation: 65W (case at 25°C, on a heatsink)
Emitter to GND; load between the positive supply (for example 12V) and the Collector.
Arduino pin to the Base through a 1KΩ resistor for loads up to about 1A, or 470Ω for heavier loads. Base current stays at a few mA, safe for the pin.
For motors, relays and solenoids, add a 1N4007 diode across the load, cathode to the positive supply.
Connect the Arduino GND to the load supply GND.
Run a DC motor at about half speed with PWM on pin 9:

A Darlington drops about 1 to 2V when on, so at 2A it dissipates roughly 2 to 4W. Without a heatsink a TO-220 handles only about 2W, so use a heatsink for currents above about 1A. The tab is the Collector: insulate it if the heatsink touches other parts.

blocks.text: NE555 is a Pulse Frequency Duty Cycle Adjustable Module Square Wave Signal Generator. The output frequency range is selectable. The 555 timer IC is an integrated circuit (chip) used in a variety of timer, pulse generation, and oscillator applications. The 555 can be used to provide time delays, as an oscillator, and as a flip-flop element. Derivatives provide up to four timing circuits in one package. Introduced in 1971 by Signetics, the 555 is still in widespread use due to its ease of use, low price, and stability. It is now made by many companies in the original bipolar and also in low-power CMOS types.

blocks.text: If you want to add some visual output to your Arduino projects, you’ll need a display. If you need only a little to display, the LCD1604 Parallel LCD Display with IIC/I2C interface is a quite good solution.

The I2C is a type of serial bus developed by Philips, which uses two bidirectional lines, called SDA (Serial Data Line) and SCL (Serial Clock Line). Both must be connected via pulled-up resistors. The usage voltages are standard as 5V and 3.3V.

If you already have the I2C adapter soldered onto the board like in this product, the wiring is quite easy. You should usually have only four pins to hook up. VCC and GND of course. This display works with 5 Volts. So we go for the 5V Pin.

The MPU6050 devices combine a 3-axis gyroscope and a 3-axis accelerometer on the same silicon together with an onboard Digital Motion Processor (DMP) capable of processing complex 9-axis MotionFusion algorithms.

The parts’ integrated 9-axis MotionFusion algorithms access external magnetometers or other sensors through an auxiliary master I2C bus, allowing the devices to gather a full set of sensor data without intervention from the system processor. Are the devices offered in the same 4x4x0.9 mm QFN footprint and pinout as the current MPU-3000? the family of integrated 3-axis gyroscopes, providing a simple upgrade path and making it easy to fit on space-constrained boards.

The InvenSense Motion Apps Platform that comes with the MPU-6050 abstracts motion-based complexities, offloads sensor management from the operating system and provides a structured set of APIs for application development. For precision tracking of both fast and slow motions, the parts feature a user-programmable gyro full-scale range of ±250, ±500, ±1000, and ±2000°/sec (DPS) and a user-programmable accelerometer full-scale range of ±2g, ±4g, ±8g, and ±16g.

The HMC5883 is a surface mount multi-chip module designed for low field magnetic sensing with a digital interface for applications such as low-cost compassing and magnetometry. The HMC5883 includes our state-of-the-art, high-resolution HMC118X series magneto-resistive sensors plus Honeywell developed ASIC containing amplification, automatic degaussing strap drivers, offset cancellation, 12-bit ADC that enables 1° to 2°compass heading accuracy. Applications for the HMC5883 include Mobile Phones, Netbooks, Consumer Electronics, Auto Navigation Systems, and Personal Navigation Devices.

This precision sensor is the best low-cost sensing solution for measuring barometric pressure and temperature. Because pressure changes with altitude you can also use it as an altimeter! Using the sensor is easy.

The BMP180 is the next generation of sensors and replaces the BMP085. The good news is that it is completely identical to the BMP085 in terms of firmware/software – you can use our BMP085 tutorial and any example code/libraries as a drop-in replacement. The XCLR pin is not physically present on the BMP180 so if you need to know that data is ready you will need to query the I2C bus.

blocks.text: The 7448 (74LS48) is a BCD-to-7-segment decoder/driver for common cathode displays. It converts a 4-bit BCD number (0 to 9) on inputs A to D into the seven segment signals a to g, so one chip and four data lines are enough to show a digit. Its outputs are active HIGH with internal pull-up resistors, and it includes lamp test, blanking and ripple-blanking inputs for multi-digit displays.

Outputs: 7 (a to g), active HIGH with internal pull-ups

Pin 9: e, pin 10: d, pin 11: c, pin 12: b, pin 13: a, pin 14: g, pin 15: f, pin 16: VCC
Connect outputs a to g to the matching segments and the display common cathode to GND.
Tie LT, RBI and BI/RBO to 5V (HIGH) for normal operation.
Drive A, B, C, D from four Arduino pins, or from a counter such as the 74192 or 7490.

blocks.text: The dual-channel 24 Bit Precision A/D weight Pressure Sensor Load Cell Amplifier and ADC HX711 Module is a small breakout board; for the HX711 IC that allows you to easily read load cells to measure weight. By connecting the module to your microcontroller you will be able to read the changes in the resistance of the load cell; and with some calibration. You’ll be able to get very accurate weight measurements.

This can be handy for creating your own industrial scale, process control, or simple presence detection. The HX711 Weighing Sensor uses a two-wire interface (Clock and Data) for communication. Any microcontroller’s GPIO pins should work and numerous libraries have been written making it easy to read data from the HX711.
Load cells use a four-wire Wheatstone bridge to connect to the HX711. These are commonly colour RED, BLK, WHT, GRN, and YLW.
To know HX711 Datasheet visit attachment.
Each colour corresponds to the conventional colour coding of load cells :

The YLW pin acts as an optional input that not hook up to the strain gauge; but is utilized to ground and shield against outside EMI (electromagnetic interference). Please keep in mind that some load cells might have variations in colour-coding.

name: Load Cell Weight Sensor 10kg
desc: Measures weight/force up to 10 kg with high precision Uses strain gauge technology with 4-wire Wheatstone bridge Made from durable aluminum alloy for reliable performance Easy to interface with HX711 24-bit ADC module for Arduino Operates on 5-10V driving voltage Compact design, simple installation with screw mount Ideal for electronic weighing scales and force measurement applications

blocks.text: This straight bar load cell (sometimes called a strain gauge) can translate up to 10 kg of pressure (force) into an electrical signal. Each load cell is able to measure the electrical resistance that changes in response to, and proportional of, the strain (e.g. pressure or force) applied to the bar.

With this gauge, you will be able to tell just how heavy an object is, if an object’s weight changes over time, or if you simply need to sense the presence of an object by measuring strain or load applied to a surface. This straight bar load cell is made from an aluminum alloy and is capable of reading a capacity of 1KG of weight
It has Four lead wires which can be connected to HX711 A/D Pressure Sensor. It is easy to use with driving voltage 5-10V and produces the output voltage as per the force changes over it.

Installation of the Sensor is also a simple task, it needs to fix one end through the screw hole and the other end left floating state, according to the label indicates the direction of the gravitational force exerted particular attention must not directly push the white plastic cover part of the sensor in order to avoid damage.

An electronic weighing machine uses a load cell to measure the load or pressure produced by the load, here most load cells follow the method of the strain gauge, Which converts the pressure (force) into an electrical signal, these load cells have four strain gauges that are hooked up in a Wheatstone bridge formation.
When we apply to load the strain gauge resistance will change and hence the output voltage from the load cell get changes by the way we can measure the load value.
Wheatstone bridge formation of Load Cell
HX711 (24 bit Analog to Digital Converter)
HX 711 is a precision 24-bit analog to digital converter (ADC) specially designed for weighing scales and industrial control applications to interface directly with a bridge sensor.

Simply connect Load cell wires to the HX711 module based on their color, then connect DAT (Data) pin to Arduino Analog pin A1 and connect CLK (Clock) pin to Arduin0 Analog pin A0, Put Vcc and GND supply from Arduino power source pins.

blocks.text: This is YF-S201 Water Flow meter Measurement Sensor with 1-30Leter/min Flow Rate in black colour. This sensor sits in line with your water line and contains a pinwheel sensor to measure how much liquid has moved through it. There’s an integrated magnetic hall effect sensor that outputs an electrical pulse with every revolution. The hall effect sensor is sealed from the water pipe and allows the sensor to stay safe and dry.
By counting the pulses from the output of the sensor, you can easily calculate water flow. Each pulse is approximately 2.25 millilitres.

Note this isn’t a precision sensor, and the pulse rate does vary a bit depending on the flow rate, fluid pressure, and sensor orientation. It will need careful calibration if better than 10% precision is required. However, it’s great for basic measurement tasks!

We have an example Arduino sketch(check the ATTACHMENTS tab) that is useful to quickly test the sensor; it will calculate the approximate flow of water in liters/hour. The pulse signal is a simple square wave so it’s quite easy to log and convert into liters per minute using the following formula.

This article demonstrates how to play with the u-blox NEO-6M global positioning system (GPS) module, a very popular, cost-effective, high-performance GPS module with a ceramic patch antenna, an on-board memory chip, and a backup battery that can be conveniently integrated with a broad range of microcontrollers. Nowadays, two NEO-6M GPS modules are extremely popular — the GY-GPS6MV2 and the GY-GPSV3-NEO

As indicated, the GPS modules are based on the u-blox NEO-6M GPS engine. The type number of the NEO-6M is NEO-6M-0-001, and its ROM/FLASH version is ROM 7.0.3 (PCN reference UBX-TN-11047-1). The NEO-6M module includes one configurable UART interface for serial communication, but the default UART (TTL) baud rate here is 9,600. Because the GPS signal is right-hand circular-polarized (RHCP), the style of the GPS antenna will be different from the common whip antennas used for linear polarized signals. The most popular antenna type is the patch antenna. Patch antennas are flat, generally have a ceramic and metal body, and are mounted on a metal base plate. They are often cast in a housing. For more information about u-blox reference designs, see their website. Remember, the position of the antenna mounting is very crucial for optimal performance of the GPS receiver. When using the patch antenna, it should be oriented parallel to the geographic horizon. The antenna must have full view of the sky, ensuring a direct line of sight with as many visible satellites as possible

If you are wandering to navigate the distance with a drone then this GPS Module is needed for you. GPS drones are equipped with a GPS module that allows them to know their location relative to a network of orbiting satellites. Connecting to signals from these satellites allows the drone to perform functions such as position hold, autonomous flight, return to home, and waypoint navigation.

This is a complete GPS module that is based on the NEO 6M GPS. This unit uses the latest technology to give the best possible positioning information and includes a larger built-in 25 x 25mm active GPS antenna with a UART TTL socket. A battery is also included so that you can obtain a GPS lock faster. This is an updated GPS module that can be used with ardupilot mega v2. This GPS module gives the best possible position information, allowing for better performance with your Ardupilot or other Multirotor control platform.

blocks.text: The Pro Mini ATmega328P 5V/16MHz (Blue) is a compact, low-cost Arduino-compatible development board designed for advanced users and embedded applications where space and power consumption are critical. Powered by the same ATmega328P microcontroller used in the Arduino Uno, the Pro Mini offers full Arduino functionality in a much smaller footprint, making it ideal for wearable tech, drones, data loggers, and portable IoT systems.

Operating at 5V with a 16MHz clock speed, this version of the Pro Mini is optimized for performance while maintaining compatibility with standard Arduino libraries and peripherals. It features 14 digital I/O pins (6 with PWM), 8 analog inputs, and supports UART, I2C, and SPI communication protocols.

This board comes without a built-in USB port, keeping it lightweight and compact. Users program the board via an external USB to TTL converter (FTDI or CP2102). Its minimalist design and onboard voltage regulator make it perfect for custom PCB integration and low-profile installations.
Whether you’re building a UV detection system, smart garden, or wireless sensor node, the Pro Mini ATmega328P is the ultimate choice for embedded Arduino projects.

name: 7490 Decade Counter IC
desc: 4-bit binary decade counter IC Counts from 0 to 9 (decimal) and then resets Supports asynchronous reset and preset inputs Operates at standard TTL logic levels Commonly used in digital clocks, frequency dividers, and counters

blocks.text: The 7490 (74LS90) is a 4-bit decade counter IC in a DIP-14 package. Inside are a divide-by-2 stage and a divide-by-5 stage; linked together they count from 0 to 9 in BCD and then return to 0. It is a classic part for digital clocks, frequency dividers, event counters and logic training, usually paired with a 7447 BCD-to-7-segment decoder.
Function: decade counter (divide-by-2 and divide-by-5 sections)
Clock: counts on the falling (HIGH to LOW) edge
Reset: asynchronous reset-to-0 and set-to-9 inputs
Note that the supply pins are 5 and 10, not the corners of the chip.
How to Connect as a 0 to 9 Counter
Tie pins 2, 3, 6 and 7 to GND for normal counting. Taking both R0 pins HIGH resets the count to 0.
QD (pin 11) gives the input frequency divided by 10, ready for the next counter stage.

desc: Soil Moisture Meter Sensor for Arduino 1. Sensing Method: Resistive (dual probe) 2. Output Type: Analog 3. Probe Dimension: Approx. 6cm x 3cm 4. Compatibility: Arduino and other microcontrollers

blocks.text: This is Soil Moisture Meter, Soil Humidity Sensor, Water Sensor, Soil Hygrometer for Ardunio. With this module, you can tell when your plants need watering by how moist the soil is in your pot, garden, or yard. The two probes on the sensor act as variable resistors. Use it in a home automated watering system, hook it up to IoT, or just use it to find out when your plant needs a little love. Installing this sensor and its PCB will have you on your way to growing a green thumb!

The soil moisture sensor consists of two probes which are used to measure the volumetric content of water. The two probes allow the current to pass through the soil and then it gets the resistance value to measure the moisture value.

When there is more water, the soil will conduct more electricity which means that there will be less resistance. Therefore, the moisture level will be higher. Dry soil conducts electricity poorly, so when there will be less water, then the soil will conduct less electricity which means that there will be more resistance. Therefore, the moisture level will be lower.

blocks.text: Heart Rate data can be used in many Electronic design and microcontroller projects. But the heart rate data is difficult to read, however, the Pulse Sensor Amped help us to read heart rate. The Heart Beat Pulse Sensor Amped is a plug-and-play heart-rate sensor for Arduino.
It can be used by students, artists, athletes, makers, and game & mobile developers who want to easily incorporate live heart-rate data into their projects.

Pulse Sensor Amped adds amplification and noise cancellation circuitry to the hardware. It’s noticeably faster and easier to get reliable pulse readings. Pulse Sensor Amped works with either a 3V or 5V Arduino.

Connect the sensor’s power supply pins to the Arduino board supply pin as Red – 5V, Black – GND and Purple – A0 (analog input 0) its over. This Analog input reading can be displayed in the serial terminal of Arduino IDE or it can be drawn as the pulse by using Processing IDE.
A Color-Coded Cable, with a standard male header connectors. Plug it straight into an Arduino or a Breadboard. No soldering is required.
The Pulse Sensor has 3 holes around the outside edge which make it easy to sew it into almost anything.

blocks.text: If you are wandering to build a device that detects temperature and humidity from the atmosphere, then This sensor is needed for you.

The DHT22 Digital Temperature and Humidity Sensor Module AM2302 is a basic, low-cost digital temperature and humidity sensor. It uses a capacitive humidity sensor and a thermistor to measure the surrounding air and spits out a digital signal on the data pin (no analog input pins needed).

blocks.text: If you want to make a robot which has lots of moving parts or if you want to control too many LEDs with PWM outputs, then the limited PWM outputs of your microcontroller would be a big problem for you. To overcome this problem, the only thing you should do is to get a 16-Channel 12-Bit PWM/Servo Driver.
You can control 16 free-running PWM outputs with 16-Channel 12-Bit PWM/Servo Driver using only 2 pins. You can even chain up 62 breakouts to control up to 992 PWM outputs.
It’s an I2C-controlled PWM driver with a built-in clock. That means you do not need to continuously send it to signal to tie up your microcontroller, it is completely free running!

It is 5V compliant, which means you can control it from a 3.3V microcontroller and still safely drive up to 6V outputs. This is good when you want to control white or blue LEDs with 3.4+ forward voltages. 6 address select pins so you can wire up to 62 of these on a single I2C bus, a total of 992 outputs.

blocks.text: The A4988 driver Stepper Motor Driver is a complete micro-stepping motor driver with built-in converter, easy to operate. It operates from 8 V to 35 V and can deliver up to approximately 1 A per phase without a heat sink or forced air flow (it is rated for 2 A per coil with sufficient additional cooling).
A4988 driver Stepper Motor Driver includes a fixed off-time current regulator, the regulator can be in slow or mixed decay mode. The converter is the key to the easy implementation of the A4988.

There are no phase sequence tables, the high-frequency control interface programming etc. The application of A4988 interface is very suitable for a complex microprocessor is not available or overload. In the stepping operation, the chopping control in the A4988 automatically selects the current decay mode (slow or mixed). The mix decay current control scheme can reduce the audible motor noise, increased step accuracy, and reduced power consumption.

blocks.text: The DRV8825 Stepper Motor Driver with Aluminum Heat Sink is a breakout board for TI’s DRV8825 microstepping bipolar stepper motor driver.

The module has a pinout and interface that are nearly identical to those of the A4988 stepper motor driver carriers, so it can be used as a higher-performance drop-in replacement for those boards in many applications.

The DRV8825 features adjustable current limiting, overcurrent, and overtemperature protection, and six microstep resolutions (down to 1/32-step). It operates from 8.2 – 45 V and can deliver up to approximately 1.5 A per phase without a heat sink or forced air flow (rated for up to 2.2 A per coil with sufficient additional cooling).

Note: We are supplying two DRV8825 Drivers as DRV8825 Stepper Motor Driver with Aluminum Heat Sink- Good Quality and DRV8825 Stepper Motor Driver with Aluminum Heat Sink- Normal Quality. The difference between them is, the good quality DRV8825 has more number of PCB layers and it features the connecting pins which are of gold plated as compared to other. (refer to above image)

desc: Ultra-compact design with 0.28″ bright red LED display Measures DC voltage from 0V to 100V Auto decimal point adjustment for improved readability 3-wire connection: simple setup for single or dual power sources Reverse polarity protection to prevent damage Compatible with 5V–24V working voltage Ideal for battery monitoring, automotive diagnostics, and DIY electronics

blocks.text: This is tiny and compact digital voltmeter with a red LED Display. The 0.28inch 0-100V Three Wire DC Voltmeter Red Panel requires only a few minutes of configuration and is as simple as directly connecting wires to the source you want to measure and seeing the LED blink!!!!

The red wire is to connect to the positive pole, the black wire is to connect to negative pole and the yellow/white wire is to connect to the positive pole of that source or another source across which we meant to measure the voltage. While measuring the supply voltage of another source make sure that negative pole is joined common. No need to worry even if there is any connection mismatch of the wires, the electric circuit won’t be a boom because it features reverse polarity protection.

To reach the best measurement accuracy, this voltmeter will automatically move the decimal point’s position according to the different measuring voltage. When it measures the voltage below 10V, it will display two places after the decimal point. When it measures the voltage above 10V, it will display one place after the decimal point.

This voltmeter can be used to measure the storage battery’s voltage in motorcycles and cars and also can grasp the storage battery’s status. It also can be used to measure other voltage. 30V is the voltmeter’s maximum operating limited voltage, please leave enough margin when working, to avoid voltmeter’s permanent damage because of an electrical spark, power supply ripple, or other too high abrupt change of voltage.
Very bight and decent LED Display is ready to measure the dc voltages in the range of 0V to 100V.
Red Wire: Positive of the Power supply
Black Wire: Negative of the Power supply and also used as the negative of the measurement voltage source
Yellow/White/Blue: Positive of the measurement voltage source
CASE 1: If you have only one power source to give Power as well as to measure the voltage
CASE 2: If you have to measure the voltage of another source then
Note: The display weight and Dimensions may have ±2% error.
Very small and lightweight voltmeter module.
Very handy and easy to use.
Best operates in the working voltage range of 5V to 24V

blocks.text: Almost one and half-year before Raspberry Pi Foundation had launched a revolutionary update on their Single Board Computer (SBC) Pi 3 and become the most popular Microcontroller board in the community which is known as a Raspberry Pi 4. On the same timeline, the Raspberry Pi Foundation came with a new astonishing SBC named Raspberry Pi Pico.

The main highlighted thing about RPi Pico is the Lowest cost and Smallest size development board from Raspberry Pi Foundation ever. On the technical side, it is equipped with an RP2040 Microcontroller chip developed by Raspberry Pi Foundation itself. RP2040 is their first dual-core ARM Cortex M0+ processor-based latest small-sized, budget-friendly microcontroller.

The RP2040 is supported with both C/C++ and micro-python, meaning that if you’re a beginner and want to learn any of these languages, the Raspberry Pico would be the best product option to start with.

name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance Sensor Module 2-400cm
desc: Non-contact distance measurement from 2 cm to 400 cm 5 V supply, 15 mA working current, 40 kHz Simple Trigger / Echo interface for Arduino and microcontrollers Measuring angle about 15°

blocks.text: The HC-SR04 measures distance by sending a 40 kHz ultrasonic burst and timing the echo. It needs only two digital pins (Trigger and Echo) and is widely used for obstacle detection, liquid-level and parking-sensor projects.
Range 2–400 cm with a narrow measuring angle (about 15°)
Start a reading with a 10 µs pulse on TRIG
ECHO stays high for the round-trip time of the sound
Four pins: VCC, TRIG, ECHO, GND
Distance = (ECHO high time × speed of sound) ÷ 2. With the time in microseconds, distance in cm ≈ time ÷ 58.
ECHO outputs a 5 V signal: use a voltage divider or a level converter before connecting it to 3.3 V boards such as the ESP32 or Raspberry Pi.
Soft or angled surfaces reflect less sound and can give unstable readings.
Leave at least ~60 ms between readings so old echoes do not interfere.
4-channel logic level converter · female-to-female jumper wires
Does it work with the ESP32?
Yes, power it from 5 V and reduce the ECHO signal to 3.3 V with a divider or level converter.
About 2 cm; closer objects are not measured reliably.

desc: 131 powerful instructions – Most Single Clock Cycle Execution 32 x 8 general purpose working registers Fully static operation Up to 20MIPS throughput at 20MHz On-chip 2-cycle multiplier Write/erase cycles: 10,000 flash/100,000 EEPROM Optional boot code section with independent lock bits In system programming by on-chip boot program True read while write operation Programming lock for software security Two 8-bit timer/counters with separate prescaler and compare mode One 16-bit timer/counter with separate prescaler, compare mode, and capture mode Real-time counter with separate oscillator

blocks.text: This is a Chinese version of ATmega328P-PU IC which also known as ATmega328P-U. So you may receive IC with printed name ATmega328P-U.

The ATMEGA328P- U is a low-power CMOS 8-bit microcontroller based on the AVR enhanced RISC architecture. By executing powerful instructions in a single clock cycle, the ATmega328P-PU achieves throughputs approaching 1 MIPS per MHz allowing the system designer to optimize power consumption versus processing speed.

The AVR core combines a rich instruction set with 32 general purpose working registers. All the 32 registers are directly connected to the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), allowing two independent registers to be accessed in one single instruction executed in one clock cycle. The resulting architecture is more code efficient while achieving throughputs up to ten times faster than conventional CISC microcontrollers.

The ATmega328P-PU AVR is supported with a full suite of program and system development tools including C Compilers, Macro Assemblers, Program Debugger/Simulators, In-Circuit Emulators, and Evaluation Kits.
Note: The available IC model for this type is ATMEGA328P U.

blocks.text: Mega 2560 is an Arduino board based on ATmega2560. It is one of the most advanced ATmega based Arduinos in terms of processor. It has 54 digital I/O pins. 14 of them can be used as PWM outputs. It has 16 analog inputs, 4 UART (serial ports), 16 MHz crystal oscillator, USB connection, adapter input, ICSP output and a reset button. With the Mega 2560 R3 model, the 16U2 model was used instead of the 8U2 model in the previous versions. In this way, faster data transfer is achieved using less memory.

It is compatible with all shields designed for Arduino Duemilanove and Diecimila. Thanks to more pins, we can use this advanced processor in many projects such as 3D printers that we cannot do with entry-level Arduinos such as Uno. Arduino Mega 2560 R3 is the latest model of Arduino Mega. It supports all the features found in previous models.

Arduino Mega 2560 can be powered from USB and an external adapter or battery. The power source is selected automatically. The board can be fed from an external source between 6-20V. If the supply is below 7V, the 5V output pin cannot give 5V and the board may work unbalanced. If an external power source higher than 12V is used, the voltage regulator may overheat and damage the board. It is recommended to use 7-12 Volts.

It is an open source development platform. You can easily program microcontrollers with Arduino libraries. Thanks to its analog and digital inputs, you can process analog and digital data. You can easily design systems that can interact with its environment. You can design systems by processing the received data using sensors. You can make new hardware with the outputs of the systems you designed.

name: CD4511 BCD to 7-segment Latch/Decoder/Driver
desc: CD4511 BCD to 7-segment Latch/Decoder/Driver 1. Output Type: Common-cathode 7-segment driver 2. Supply Voltage: 3V to 18V DC 3. Logic Family: 40xx series CMOS 4. Package: 16-pin DIP 5. Input Type: 4-bit BCD with latch

blocks.text: The CD4511 is a BCD-to-7-segment latch, decoder, and driver IC from the 40xx series of CMOS logic. Designed to interface binary-coded decimal (BCD) inputs with common-cathode 7-segment displays, this chip accepts a 4-bit BCD input and translates it into the appropriate segment-driving outputs to display decimal digits 0 through 9. The integrated latch allows BCD data to be held and displayed even after the input changes, freeing the system bus.

Internally, the device combines a storage latch, a BCD-to-7-segment decoder, and output drivers capable of sinking significant current for direct LED display operation. A lamp test input forces all segments on for display verification, while a blanking input can be used to suppress unwanted outputs or for multiplexing applications. The CD4511 operates across a wide voltage range, making it suitable for battery-powered instrumentation, digital clocks, and panel meters.
4-bit BCD input with integrated latch storage
Lamp test input for display verification
Blanking input for output suppression and multiplexing
High noise immunity typical of CMOS devices

name: CD4094 8-stage Shift-and-Store Bus Register
desc: CD4094 8-stage Shift-and-Store Bus Register 1. Type: 8-bit shift register with storage latch 2. Operation: Serial-in, parallel-out 3. Supply Voltage: 3V to 15V DC 4. Logic Family: 40xx series CMOS 5. Package: 16-pin DIP

blocks.text: The CD4094 is an 8-stage shift-and-store bus register from the 40xx series CMOS logic family. This device combines an 8-bit serial-in, parallel-out shift register with an 8-bit storage latch, allowing data to be shifted in serially and then latched into parallel outputs under separate control. The shift register and storage register can be updated independently, enabling double-buffered output updates without disrupting the shifting process.

Separate clock inputs control the shift register and the storage latch. Data is clocked into the shift register on the rising edge of the shift clock, while a separate strobe input transfers the shift-register contents to the output latch. A serial output allows cascading multiple CD4094 devices into longer shift registers. The CD4094 is widely used in LED displays, keypad scanning, and general-purpose I/O expansion for microcontrollers.
Storage latch with separate clock control

name: CD4067 16-channel Analog Multiplexer/Demultiplexer
desc: CD4067 16-channel Analog Multiplexer/Demultiplexer 1. Type: 16-channel analog switch 2. Address Lines: 4-bit (16 channels) 3. Supply Voltage: 3V to 15V DC 4. Logic Family: 40xx series CMOS 5. Package: 24-pin DIP

blocks.text: The CD4067 is a 16-channel analog multiplexer/demultiplexer from the 40xx series CMOS logic family. This device routes a common input/output (Z) to one of 16 independent input/output pins (I0-I15), controlled by a 4-bit binary address. The channel selected is determined by the address inputs (A0-A3), and the switch is bidirectional, allowing signals to flow in either direction.

Each channel is a CMOS transmission gate with low on-resistance and minimal signal distortion. The CD4067 can handle both analog and digital signals, with a voltage range from VEE to VDD. An enable input places all switches in a high-impedance state for bus applications. Typical applications include data acquisition systems, signal routing, audio switching, and analog-to-digital conversion front-ends.
4-bit binary address selects one of 16 channels

blocks.text: The CD4015 is a dual 4-stage static shift register IC, containing two independent 4-bit serial-in, parallel-out shift registers on a single chip.

Being static, each register retains its stored data indefinitely as long as power is applied, without needing a refresh clock, useful for expanding a limited number of control lines into more parallel outputs.
Part of the CD40xx CMOS logic family, this IC is a standard building block for serial-to-parallel data conversion circuits.

blocks.text: The L293D Motor Driver/Servo Shield for Arduino is probably one of the most versatile on the market and features 2 servo and 4 motor connectors for DC or stepper motors. That makes it a great shield for any robotic project.
